items.quote: For three years the company will deploy INR 500 crores of capital, by debt or by internal resources for these projects.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 30-35% once Town Villas and villa projects contribute largely
items.quote: Given the real estate sector, sell product of residentials and construct, build, and sell, the EBITDA margins would gradually move up around, 30%-35% once Town Villas and the villa projects contribute largely.

items.statement: Hospitality segment expected to contribute INR 50 crores+ PAT per year from third or fourth year
items.period: third or fourth year from now
items.quote: the hospitality sector would contribute say third or fourth year from now to an average of INR 50 crores of PAT per year. This represents an annuity income model, with both hotels expected to contribute INR 50 crores+.

items.statement: Target PAT margins higher than 20% over next two years
items.quote: we feel that we are comfortable and we would be able to give up a PAT margins even higher than 20% over a run of two years from now.

items.statement: Average selling price remained same at INR 7,500 per sq ft, average ticket size INR 78 lakhs per unit
items.quote: Our average selling price per square feet has also remained same at INR 7,500 per square feet which is almost similar to Q1FY26. For this first quarter of Q1 FY27, the average price of the unit which has been sold stood at INR 78 lakhs per unit.

items.statement: Average ticket size projected to reach INR 95 lakhs to INR 1 crore
items.quote: Average ticket size today we already have mentioned that it is something around INR 78 lakhs and the projections and the numbers which we have, our average ticket size goes to around INR 95 lakhs to INR 1 crore

items.statement: Premium segment below INR 5 crores seeing good traction, above INR 10 crores facing slowdown
items.quote: We have already seen in the sector that things above INR 10 crores, INR 15 crores, INR 25 crores, INR 30 crores in the city of Mumbai are facing a little slowdown. But when it comes to anything which is below INR 5 crores is what is very much keen on spends by individuals.

items.statement: Aspire to maintain 40-45% premium, 30-35% middle income, 20% affordable housing mix
items.quote: We still will have a mixed bag of it and going forward we can say that we would aspire to have 40%-45% as premium segment and around 30% - 35% as middle income group segment and 20% as affordable housing.

items.statement: No fund-raising program planned, debt-to-equity to gradually come down as projects mature
items.quote: We remain focused and confident on reducing our debt next year onwards as some of our residential projects have started nearing completion and these reductions will be partially offset by new loans which are being taken for building the annuity assets.

items.statement: Board approved raising Rs.137 Crores via CCDs, equity shares, and warrants; pending shareholder approval; funds for exploration excluding Kyrgyzstan project
items.quote: Board has approved this particular raise through CCDs, equity shares and equity warrants. And of course, we have to wait for the shareholders' approval.

items.statement: Jonnagiri expansion to 2,500 tpd processing targeting up to 2 tons gold per annum around 2029-2030
items.quote: we are going to increase it to 2,500 tons per day, which actually would take us at some point in time to 2 tons of gold, up to 2 tons of gold, that is the maximum anticipated from this project, 2 tons of gold per annum from this project, that could happen somewhere around 29 or 30.

items.statement: Altyn Tor first phase revised mine design and life of mine plan by October 2026; underground resources expected >5 tons adding 6-7 years mine life
items.quote: The first phase revised mine design and life of mine plan we are going to deliver by October 2026 and we are expecting that the underground resources are going to be more than 5 tons.

items.statement: Due diligence on 3 new gold assets targeting production by 2028; one in Kyrgyzstan (~10 tons) offered by government
items.quote: these assets once acquired could come into the production in the year 2028 at least by end of 2027 or 2028, that is the kind of strategy we have for the gold portfolio.

items.statement: Bhalukona Ni-Cu-PGE project planning 3,000 tpd processing plant; feasibility by mid-2027; significant capex expected from fund raise
items.quote: We are thinking of about 3000 tons per day processing plant, which effectively means this plant would be even bigger than what is going to be set up in Jonnagiri.

items.statement: Logrosan Tungsten preliminary resource modeling by early October 2026; targeting ~1,000 tpd plant and 3Mt resource for 10-year mine life
items.quote: preliminary resource modeling will be completed by early October and we will announce it to the market.

items.statement: Mozambique Li-Cs-Ta drilling 1,500-2,000m starting mid-September 2026; targeting 200 tpd concentrate plant by end-2027 or Q1 2028
items.quote: we aim to set up a 200 ton per day processing plant to concentrate lithium and tantalum by the end of 2027.

items.statement: Tungsten prices have risen significantly due to demand in space, defense, high-speed steel; Tantalum demand growing with semiconductor industry
items.quote: People have realized the importance of tungsten, which is used primarily in space technology and also in high speed steel and so on and so forth. In the defense industry, it is pretty much used. So the price also has gone up.

items.statement: Ganajur project pending court verdict; relying on recent Gadchiroli precedent restoring pre-2015 rights; government may grant leeway for near-production assets
items.quote: After two years of delay, the hearings have started before the court went to the summer vacation in the month of May there were some hearings and then subsequently the hearings were expected in the month of July.

items.statement: Jonnagiri Q1: 112 kg dore produced, 90 kg bullion, 59 kg sold for Rs.87 Cr revenue, Rs.25 Cr PAT; 80 kg gold equivalent in stock
items.quote: We sold about 59 kilos of gold and that has given about Rs.87 Crores of revenue and there is a profit after tax of Rs.25 Crores and Deccan's share of Rs.6.35 Crores has come into our books.

items.statement: Gold price arbitrage: selling more at ~Rs.1,50,000 per 10 grams to maximize revenue
items.quote: if you look at the previous quarter to the current quarter, last time the price was slightly low whereas now in this quarter the price is pretty good. I mean you might be seeing that it is like almost like Rs.1,50,000 per 10 grams.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to stabilize at 65-70% after 1-2 more quarters as gold sales catch up with production
items.quote: So, to stabilize to about 65%, 70% of EBITDA, I believe it will take another quarter or two. That is how it is going to be and really this coming quarter is something with a lot of gold in the stock and also the production upgradation that is going to happen in terms of grade, not in terms of the plantr anything.

items.statement: Battery storage demand in India to grow significantly over next 10 years; Adani and others building large storage facilities driving need for battery metals
items.quote: In fact, even some of our partners are setting up like even they are setting up large storage facilities and of course the largest being done by Adani group of industries. So battery storage is going to be a very, very prominent feature in the next 10 years and that battery storage would require so much of battery rela

items.statement: Physical AGM confirmed for Mumbai this year after 5-6 years of virtual meetings
items.quote: Yes, Imran, you are quite a physical AGM. I think this year we will, I guarantee you we will have it in Mumbai. That will be a physical because in the last five, six years, we have also not met many of them.

items.statement: Capex guidance: INR11,000-11,500 crores over next 2 years, INR15,000-20,000 crores in year 3
items.quote: we should be at around INR11,000 crores -- close to INR11,000 crores for the next 2 years and a bit higher, around between INR15,000 crores to INR20,000 crores in the year after that

items.statement: Copper JV requires $300M+ capex over next 9 months, targeting Q1 FY28 operational
items.quote: it would take a total capex of around $300-plus million to get it to completion. So as of now, we have done part of it, and we intend to complete that capex over the period of next 9 months

items.statement: Thriveni Odisha volumes to grow 39% YoY to 34-35 million tons in FY27 with new mines
items.quote: we expect Odisha volumes to grow 39% year-on-year to 34 million to 35 million tons in FY '27

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin hit record 39.2% in Q1 FY27, up 639bps YoY and 631bps QoQ
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin came in at 39.2%, the best margins the company has ever reported. Importantly, this has scaled on both fronts, up 639 basis points year-on-year and up 631 basis points quarter-on-quarter

items.statement: Slurry pipeline saves INR550/ton on pellet costs; export mix at 25% of pellet sales
items.quote: The slurry pipeline saving is around INR900 -- INR700 a ton, and that will remain -- sorry, INR550 a ton, that will remain

items.statement: Pellet plant reached 100% capacity utilization within 4 months; 1.69M tons produced in Q1
items.quote: Pellets production was 1.69 million tons, reaching 100% capacity utilization within 4 months of the second plant coming on stream in May

items.statement: Chemaf debt restructuring to complete next quarter, expected 40-50% reduction in consolidated debt
items.quote: it will come down by near about, I mean, 40% to 50%

items.statement: NTPC wage receivable of INR300+ crores not provided for; arbitration won, matter subjudice, resolution expected in 2-3 months
items.quote: In arbitration, we had won this award. And since NTPC does not go for -- accept the arbitration, the matter is again subjudice still now. And we are hopeful in the next 2, 3 months, NTPC matter would be resolved

items.statement: BHQ beneficiation plant on track for March 2028 commissioning with 38% recovery, 16-17M tons annual output
items.quote: In BHQ, we hope to commission it by March '28 as per our original schedule. The recovery of 38% against original 35% is more or less confirmed

items.statement: Thriveni raising INR650 crores to replace high-cost debt, fund capex and overseas subsidiary investments
items.quote: we just wanted to reduce our high-cost debt. And at the same time, we are going for capex, capital investment, and we have to invest in our outside subsidiaries also for doing the MDO contract

items.statement: Revised FY27 Lamination volume target to 82,000 tons from 78,000 tons
items.quote: As our recently concluded Capex comes on stream, we are confident of achieving significant growth in the remaining year. Therefore, we are revising our annual target to 82,000 tons for Lamination from 78,000 tons, as previously stated in Q4 Conference Call.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA target of roughly ₹370 crores based on current outlook
items.quote: If I start from current year, I would look at an EBITDA of roughly ₹ 370-odd crores based on current outlook.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target above ₹2,500 crores at 90,000 ton operating level with 17-17.2% EBITDA margin
items.quote: For the next year, we should be looking at a turnover above about ₹ 2,500 crores if we don't do the Capex. I am obviously going to talk ex of the incremental Capex on Lamination. So, at a 90,000 ton operating level, we should be looking at a ₹ 2,500 crores turnover and an EBITDA margin of about 17%-17.2%.

items.statement: ₹150 crore Capex completed, increasing sheet metal capacity to 108,000 tons and augmenting Casting and Machining
items.quote: We have recently commenced operations of the previously announced ₹ 150 crores Capex, which was announced last year, increasing our sheet metal capacity to 108,000 tons and augmenting our Casting and Machining capacity.

items.statement: ₹290 crore Greenfield Casting facility in Hyderabad underway, ₹60 crore spent, commissioning by Q1 FY30
items.quote: We are now progressing with the ₹ 290 crores investment for our Greenfield Casting facility in Hyderabad. This facility will help consolidate our foundry operations and provide the infrastructure required for the next phase of growth.

items.statement: Potential ₹200 crore Bangalore facility and ₹200 crore equipment Capex for FY28-29 to reach ₹3,000-3,300 crore revenue
items.quote: If I were to assume that we go ahead and make a facility in Bangalore, that would entail a Capex of roughly about ₹ 200-odd crores. Then in terms of another equipment, about ₹ 200-odd crores. So, ₹ 400 crores plus the ₹ 290 crores, which we have announced, would be capable of taking us to a top-line of closer to about

items.statement: Strong visibility in Mining, Oil & Gas, Railways, Metros, Off-highway, Specialty industrial, and Data Centers
items.quote: Beyond Data Centers, we are seeing strong visibility in railways, metros, Mining and off-highway equipment, and specialty end-use applications in industrial sector.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 Adjusted EBITDA margin 16.8%, expected to improve as operating leverage kicks in from new capacity
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.8% for the quarter.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin target of 18-18.5% as Casting/Machining Capex comes online and value-added mix increases
items.quote: No, for sure it will be upwards of 18% for sure. With the Capex on the Casting and Machining coming online and the value-added products increasing as well as the co-drop products increasing, your margins should be closer to 18%-18.5%.

items.statement: LPG cost increases being passed through to customers
items.quote: Whatever is the incremental cost obviously is being incurred by the company, and it is being compensated by the customers as well.

items.statement: Data Center demand strong from Cummins, Marathon, Nidec; measured approach due to AI investment sustainability concerns
items.quote: We are seeing strong demand from customers such as Cummins, Marathon, Nidec, and are also developing opportunities with a couple of more marquee customers, at the same time, we remain mindful that the pace of AI Data Center investments may not be sustainable indefinitely.

items.statement: High value-added assemblies (Integrated Rotor Shaft, Stator) grew faster than loose laminations, driven by Data Centers, Mining, Off-highway, Wind
items.quote: Importantly, within Lamination, Higher Value-Added Assemblies, including Integrated Rotor Shaft and Stator Assemblies, grew faster than loose Lamination. This reflects a continued improvement in the product mix and increasing contribution from value-added offerings.

items.statement: Mining and Oil & Gas segments can correct quickly; Data Center growth pace uncertain; Capex timed to demand visibility
items.quote: If I just look at the outlook and the demand forecast from the customers, we do see that kind of growth over the next three years. But it is coming from segments which, I would say, can change very quickly. So, like Mining and Oil & Gas are segments which go up very fast and can correct very fast. And Data Center is ob

items.statement: Net debt ₹491 crores; potential ₹25-30 crore working capital optimization; no immediate debt reduction target due to ongoing Capex
items.quote: Right now, the net debt is somewhere around ₹ 491 crores as of last quarter end. We have already incurred, like I said, about ₹ 60 odd crores of expenditure out of the ₹ 290 crores. Despite that, we have been able to meaningfully reduce the net debt, and I think there is still potential to further rationalize our worki

items.statement: Capex limited to maintenance and organic requirements; no expansion capex for new verticals
items.quote: We're keeping our capex limited to just maintenance and organic capex requirements, which is why I keep saying that all of these things are using our existing campus and infrastructure.

items.statement: US demand altered by tariff uncertainty and inflation; FTAs with UK/EU expected to help in medium term
items.quote: the tariff piece has stabilized and the FTA piece should offer some opportunities. But as I said, the domestic markets will also open up for us vis-a-vis our new product verticals

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 16% due to lower revenue, mix changes, and raw material inflation
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA came in at INR101 crores. The EBITDA margin came in at about 16%, again, primarily driven by slightly lower revenues, some tweaks in product mix and some inflationary headwinds on the raw material front.

items.statement: India to become largest or top-2 revenue jurisdiction in medium term via new verticals
items.quote: in the medium term, India will probably become the largest jurisdiction for the company going forward, if not the largest, amongst the top 2.

items.statement: No specific FY27 growth/margin guidance given; management says domestic demand positive, exports recovering, margins follow top line
items.quote: To give guidance is challenging in the current environment, there are so many factors out of control. But generally speaking, it is looking quite positive from where we sit today for the domestic as well as exports overall is alright, margins follow the top line typically.

items.statement: FY27 non-separator capex budget INR 100 crore; separator project adds INR 30-40 crore this year, total FY27 capex INR 100-150 crore
items.quote: In FY27, we have about INR 100 crore budget and this does not include the separator. The separator spend will be over the course of the next 1.5 years. So this year, it will be probably more like the land cost and then everything else will pretty much be in next year's cost. So this will go up based on the separator an

items.statement: Flexible packaging growing faster but lower EBITDA margin than folding cartons; overall mix healthy, margin trajectory uncertain structurally
items.quote: The flexible packaging is a lower-margin business generally speaking. The returns are similar profile-wise, return on capital and all, which is really what matters. But the EBITDA margins tend to be lower. So obviously as the flexible grows, it can reduce the Company margin. But so far, the carton has also grown and th

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance around INR2,000 crores
items.quote: And this year is expected around about INR2,000 crores of revenue.

items.statement: Senior Living presales target of INR1,500 crores by FY29-30
items.quote: FY 29-30 target is actually to look at INR1,500 crores of presales from Senior Living itself.

items.statement: Medium-term presales target of INR3,000-4,000 crores to sustain ROE
items.quote: In the medium term, maybe INR3,000 crores, INR4,000 crores of presales we will need to hit.

items.statement: FY27 capex budget of INR800 crores including INR180 crores deployed in Q1
items.quote: We have a total budget of deploying about INR800 crores in this financial year, including about INR180 crores that got deployed in the last quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 bookings INR358 crores, 3.6 lakh sq ft across 234 units; July YTD presales INR859 crores
items.quote: The company recorded a booking value of INR358 crores during the quarter gone by, with 3.6 lakh square feet of area sold across 234 units.

items.statement: Target project-level gross margin ~30%, SG&A ~12%, PBT ~18%, PAT ~12-13%
items.quote: As we generally target about a 30% gross profit margin at the project level, about a 12% SG&A and 18% PBT margin and 12-13% PAT margin.

items.statement: Anmol Phase 3 and Amarah Phase 1 blended gross margin in mid-20s%
items.quote: Blended across both those projects, we should be in the mid-20s.

items.statement: Average realization improved 37% YoY to INR9,923/sq ft in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Average realization also improved significantly to INR9,923 per square foot, representing a 37% year-on-year increase, driven by a favorable product mix and continued pricing resilience across our portfolio.

items.statement: NCD redemption of INR31.25 crores (25% of issue) in Q1 FY27; Vadgaon land partly funded via NCDs to landlords
items.quote: We also commenced the redemption of NCDs issued to ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund during the quarter, INR31.25 crores, representing 25% of the original issue was redeemed.

items.statement: Revised FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 14-16% from earlier 12-13%
items.quote: Overall growth percentage from 12% to 13% may become almost around 14% to 16% overall for the whole of the current financial year, yes.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR 700-800 crores for capacity expansion in formulations, API, biotech
items.quote: So largely, I think almost around INR700 crores to INR800 crores in current year will go in the CapEx side itself.

items.statement: US business (Ipca+Unichem) expected to grow 15-17% annually over next few years
items.quote: Maybe around 15%, 16%, 17% kind of growth is possible, but currently looking at portfolio and other things.

items.statement: Management targets 15-20% revenue CAGR over next 3-5 years
items.quote: And the idea is that how we should grow between 15% to 20% CAGR in next 3 to 5 years. Management is committed for that number, and we are planning to do every bit in our scope to see that we achieve that growth.

items.statement: Annual EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 40-42%
items.quote: But annualized basis, 40% to 42% margins are sustainable.

items.statement: Seamec ANANT to resume ONGC IMR contract after ~1 month statutory formalities
items.quote: But due to some statutory formalities that we need to comply with, it may take almost like a month before it resumes its contract with ONGC. We will try to expedite this process as much as possible. But we are hopeful that it will start the operation within this quarter.

items.statement: Strong DSV demand expected for next 3-5 years, especially if Iran sanctions lift
items.quote: So for next 3 to 5 years, we remain quite bullish that DSVs are going to get a strong demand.

items.statement: Middle East (Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Abu Dhabi) identified as key growth markets
items.quote: Middle East as a whole is a very good opportunity. Saudi Arabia is a hotspot, then Qatar is a hotspot, then Abu Dhabi is also an hotspot. So there are a lot of opportunity in these 3 countries.

items.statement: Fleet contract mix: 35-40% short-term (EPC), balance mid-to-long term (IMR)
items.quote: See, around 35% to 40% contracts are short term and balance are on long-term. Basically, the EPC contracts that Naveenji mentioned are short term and IMR are generally mid- to long term.

items.statement: Samudra Manthan policy impact visible only after 3-5 years due to long gestation
items.quote: No, 2 years will be too short a time because it is going to take, as I told you, it is 3 to 5 years to get a visible impact for Seamec because oil exploration activity is a long gestation kind of activity.

items.statement: Gallant vessel sale expected to complete in September post shareholder approval
items.quote: So, post-shareholder approval, I don't think so there will be much formalities. And in the coming month, which is September, we should be able to complete.

items.statement: MOU with DG Shipping for INR 1,000 crore fleet growth over 2 years on track with ANANT acquisition
items.quote: So definitely, this is an MOU that we have signed knowing well our growth plans.

items.statement: Seamec Princess and Seamec III EPC contracts in advanced talks for post-monsoon deployment
items.quote: No, no, the talks are going on and it is at quite advanced stage. So once it is finalized, we will be filing with the exchange so that everybody is aware about the contracts.

items.statement: Seamec II charter ending August; evaluating redeployment for EPC work
items.quote: It will be completing its charter sometime in August end. And after that, we intend to use the vessel again for the EPC kind of work from -- instead of IMR work.

items.statement: FY27 branded alco-bev revenue growth guided at 60-70% YoY, with H2 as principal driver contributing 60-65% of annual branded revenue
items.quote: We expect our branded alco-bev business to grow approximately 60% to 70% for the full year, which is what we had indicated when we had done the Q4 call. With the second half expected to be the principal growth driver, in the last year it contributed nearly 60% to 65% of the annual branded alco-bev revenue.

items.statement: FY27 company-level revenue growth target of approximately 60% YoY
items.quote: At the company level we continue to target approximately 60% revenue growth year-on-year.

items.statement: FY27 company-level EBITDA margin guided at 23-24% range
items.quote: We remain confident in our ability to deliver a company-level EBITDA margin in the range of 23% to 24% for FY27, while continuing to invest behind our brands, new product launches, distribution capabilities, and international expansion.

items.statement: No large capex planned for FY27; only routine maintenance and upgrade capex as heavy capex cycle completed
items.quote: There is no large capex planned this year. Yes in the ordinary course the capex which goes into improving facilities and upgradation only that will be there. Mostly all the heavy capex has already been executed.

items.statement: Chhattisgarh distillery revenue guidance of Rs 300-400 crore for FY27 maintained despite delayed start
items.quote: We gave a guidance in Q4 where we said that between I think 300 crores to 400 crores would be the revenue from Chhattisgarh this year. And I think we are well on the road we will be able to achieve that guidance definitely.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved 30 bps YoY to 18.5%; full-year margin expected to reach 23-24% as H2 revenue scales and brand mix improves
items.quote: As we said earlier that our overall EBITDA margin in a full year basis will be on the same level or slightly better than the last year.

items.statement: Premium/super-premium/luxury portfolio grew 47.3% to Rs 82.3 crore, now 43.5% of distillery revenue vs 37.8% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our premium, super premium, and luxury portfolio grew 47.3% to 82 crores, raising its contribution to 43.5% of distillery revenue compared with 37.8% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Indri single malt growing 18-20% YoY with 87,000 filled barrels (1.6 crore litres) maturing, sufficient for multi-year growth
items.quote: For your question, we have 87,000 barrels of malt filled as on date. That is the largest in the country. And we do not see any constraints coming in from supply side.

items.statement: Camikara and Cashmir expected to grow triple-digit percentages in FY27 from small base, targeting 1 lakh+ cases each within 2-3 years
items.quote: Camikara and Cashmir this year are expecting, because see, the base is small, so they are going to see probably triple digit numbers grow.

items.statement: Ethanol policy uncertainty noted; Chhattisgarh ethanol sales dependent on government orders expected from Q2/Q3
items.quote: The reason for that is because see a lot of if you talk about ethanol the policy is very it's guided by the government and the thoughts right now. So you know to give a number there would be unfair because that's not in our control at all.

items.statement: Input cost pressures from grain and fuel prices affecting distillery margins; branded portfolio insulated due to premium pricing
items.quote: But if you see the distillery division there's been some cost pressures because of the war and internally as grain prices and fuel prices have been surging. So there has been some pressure been felt across the country because of that as well.

items.statement: Sugar division demerger scheme filed April 28, 2026; process progressing well
items.quote: We have given last quarter update that we have filed demerger of our sugar division, update on that the scheme was filed to stock exchange on 28th April 2026 and we are progressing well and so the process is continued.

items.statement: International expansion targeting 70% export / 30% domestic mix long-term; North America is largest export market currently
items.quote: So we ultimately want to have 70% export and 30% domestic. But that goal will is a few years away. But we are actively working on opening new geographies and as you understand the windows of each country start with the duty fees in the airports.

items.statement: Debt reduced by Rs 10 crore in Q1 FY27; no debt increase planned for FY27; significant debt reduction expected from FY28 as capex cycle completes
items.quote: So in this quarter we have reduced the debt by about 10 crores, but as you would understand that you know our growth trajectory continues, right? So we plan to not to increase the debt this year and all the cash from operation will be reinvested into growth and the gap.

items.statement: Defence revenue target for FY27 is INR300-350 crores with EBITDA margin of 30-35%
items.quote: In all, company aims to achieve INR300 crores to INR350 crores target this year with a marked EBITDA of 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth guidance maintained at 15-20% for FY27
items.quote: We maintain our guidance that it should be 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Defence order book of INR307 crores (INR255 cr + INR52 cr) to be executed over 10 months and 3 months respectively
items.quote: Goodluck Defence and Aerospace Limited received an order of INR255 crores for 155 mm long-range, ready-to-fill empty shells to be executed over 10 months. In addition, it received an order of INR52 crores for 20,000 155 mm shell with execution over 3 months.

items.statement: Defence EBITDA margin guided at 30-35% range; Q1 FY27 Defence EBITDA margin was 38% on INR80 cr revenue
items.quote: Margins, it is a range bound. What is the 30% to 35% range bound margin should be there as we expect.

items.statement: Value-added products at ~60% of mix, targeting increase; hydraulic tube utilization at 60-65% in Q1, ramping up rapidly
items.quote: Value-added, we have almost 60% we are already there. And in the coming years, this will increase and the legacy business, it will get reduced due to the increase in the value-added business.

items.statement: Input cost risk high due to geopolitical volatility affecting petroleum products and logistics; West Asia crisis impacting operations
items.quote: Input cost risk is very high because war is going up and down. We never know when the war will start, when the war will stop. So all the petroleum products get volatile and the petroleum products are in every product.

items.statement: Defence expansion delayed 6-9 months due to financial closure; commercialization expected by Q4 FY28, taking capacity to ~350,000 shells/year
items.quote: Basically, it is a financial closure. Now the financial closure is being done nowadays. So as soon as the financial closure is over, we will start the ramping of the production as we had said. So that is why there is a delay due to the financial closure of the project.

items.statement: Defence IPO targeted within 18 months, subject to approvals
items.quote: We hope that 18 months from today, it should be the time. But however, again, it will depend on the approvals and the systems.

items.statement: Export growth 53% in Q1 FY27 from US and Europe; pipeline healthy but geopolitical uncertainty remains
items.quote: Was around 53% -- for this quarter, the pipeline of orders is pretty healthy for this quarter also. But again, geopolitical is a factor which should not be kept aside that we have to continuously monitor.

items.statement: Targets ~10% revenue growth in FY27 with significant H2 contribution; expects 15% growth in FY28
items.quote: Based on the visibility we have today, we remain confident of achieving approximately 10% revenue growth in FY27 with a significant portion of this growth expected to come through in the second half of the financial year.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins to remain in 13-14% range for FY27
items.quote: Current year estimates which is there is around 10% growth with EBITDA of 13%-14% with similar interest cost every quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at Rs 14,636 cr as of June 30, 2026; expects execution over 3 years with book-to-bill ~3x
items.quote: As of June 30, FY26, our consolidated order book stood at Rs. 14,636 crores.

items.statement: May need Rs 100-200 cr additional working capital borrowings for execution acceleration; to be funded via internal accruals, asset monetization, project debt
items.quote: Plus, maybe some working capital borrowings of Rs. 100 crores – Rs. 200 crores may be needed in between.

items.statement: Targets Rs 150-200 cr non-core asset monetization in FY27; sold 27-acre Telangana land parcel for Rs 26 cr in Q1
items.quote: This year, target for non-core is between Rs. 150 crores to Rs. 200 crores. That we are fairly confident to achieve.

items.statement: Promoter pledge at 85-90%; expects 15-20% reduction in FY27; arbitration recoveries uncertain as PSUs pursue litigation
items.quote: Right now, if I am not mistaken, around 85% to 90% of the shares are pledged. So, we expect that to come down by at least 15%-20%.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Hydropower 68%, Irrigation 15%, Tunneling 13%, Roads/Urban 4%; order book mix similar at 62% Hydro, 17% Irrigation, 4% Tunneling, 17% Roads/Urban
items.quote: Revenue breakup sector-wise: Hydropower contributed to 68%, Irrigation 15%, Tunneling 13%, Roads, Urban Infrastructure and others 4%.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded: Long-term to A stable from A-, short-term to A1 from A2 in June 2026
items.quote: In June, our long-term credit rating was upgraded to A stable from A-, while our short-term rating was upgraded to A1 from A2.

items.statement: No exceptional items expected in FY27; prior year exceptionals from Vivaad-Se-Vishwas settlements and investment write-downs
items.quote: We don't anticipate exceptional items coming this year. That was mostly on account of last year for Vivaad-Se-Vishwas settlements and some write-down of investments.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM growth guidance of 25-30% for FY27
items.quote: Our expectation for growth of gold loan this year is around 30%, because some quarters are as per season, some quarters are off seasons. We expect that to be some between 25%-30%.

items.statement: Gold loan yield expected to stabilize around 18% with +/- 25 bps range
items.quote: We expect the yield to be somewhere around 18%. It may go down by 25 basis points or go up by 25 basis. Beyond that, we do not expect anything. It will be around 18%.

items.statement: Microfinance AUM to be contained below 10% of consolidated AUM
items.quote: I will tell at the group level, we want to contain microfinance at below 10% at a consolidated level.

items.statement: Plan to open 500 new branches in FY27 for gold loan business
items.quote: We have the plan to open around 500 branches now. We are at stream now already, progressing in that stream.

items.statement: Strong gold loan demand momentum continuing in July-August with customer and tonnage growth
items.quote: This first quarter, despite seasonally being slow, we had a good momentum, and we continue to build on that momentum in July and August as well, both from a customer perspective and from a tonnage perspective as well.

items.statement: Vehicle finance lending temporarily stopped; focus on collections with GNPA at 13.3%
items.quote: We have temporarily stopped the vehicle lending, vehicle finance. We are focusing on collection. Our collections are improving because of the improved focus.

items.statement: New MD & CEO Ashish Singh to join by January 1, 2027 with 25 years retail banking experience
items.quote: Mr. Ashish Singh has been appointed as the MD and CEO and expected to join by January 1st of 2027. He is a seasoned banker with over 25 years of experience in the retail banking space.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR 1 per share declared for Q1 FY27
items.quote: The Board has declared an interim dividend of INR1 for this quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated capital adequacy ratio at 21.29%; net worth INR 16,552 crores as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: Our capital position is strong and company is well capitalized with a capital adequacy ratio of 21.29%. The company's consolidated net worth stands at INR16,552 crores as of June 30, 2026.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 sales volume grew 3%, value grew 24%; EBITDA margin expanded 360 bps to 11.6%; expects mid-single-digit volume growth and to maintain or improve 11%+ EBITDA margin for FY27
items.quote: We maintain that the EBITDA margins delivered in this quarter would be maintained, and we are trying to better our EBITDA margins, which we have delivered in last quarter and on this quarter.

items.statement: Announced 9+ million sqm greenfield plant in South with INR 220 crore outlay, operational by Q3/Q4 FY28; plus INR 55 crore for balancing equipment across plants by Q3 FY27; total FY27 capex ~INR 275 crore, 65-70% internally funded
items.quote: So from now to '27 end, we have already looked at approximately INR275 crores outlay, which includes the INR220 crores plant plus balancing equipment in various other plants and some more balancing equipment in the Bathware, sanitaryware plant.

items.statement: Standalone capacity utilization rose from 72% to 83% YoY; JVs swung from INR 10 cr loss to INR 3 cr profit in Q1; targets 12%+ EBITDA margin
items.quote: My margins really have not gone up because of pricing. My margins have gone up because of operational efficiency that we are producing 100% in our own plants and also our JV losses have come down.

items.statement: Implemented 16-17% average price hike in Q1 to pass through gas cost increases; blended natural gas cost ~INR 68/scm (North INR 68-69, South/Morbi mid-70s); gas prices still rising marginally in July-August
items.quote: We took a price hike of -- you can take an average of about 16%, 17%.

items.statement: May-June demand decent; July resilient despite rains; expects mid-single-digit volume growth for FY27; channel inventory lean due to gas price volatility
items.quote: Demand is looking good. Let's not forget that in the last 30 months, prices had reduced also by 15%, 16%. So that's been the price increase. So from that point of view, because of that scenario, it's been well accepted in the market. And demand seems to be absolutely good.

items.statement: Adding 4-5 million sqm capacity via balancing equipment in Bahadurgarh, Gujarat, Morbi, South by Q3/Q4 FY27, focused on value-added products; project sales to rise 3-4% from current 17-19% of revenue
items.quote: All put together, we will be adding another 4 million to 5 million for the mid -- this will be ready from mid-quarter 3 and would be completely in place in quarter 4. This would add, not only capacity, but also will add value-added mix.

items.statement: Morbi exports down 50-60% from peak due to geopolitics/freight; expected to persist this quarter; domestic dumping risk low due to high gas costs
items.quote: The only negative in the quarter has been from a Morbi perspective is exports has been down due to geopolitical reasons, the export is down a good 50%, 60% from the peak.

items.statement: Current revenue run-rate ~INR 3,700 crore at today's prices with existing capacity; balancing equipment could add ~INR 300 crore; new South plant adds INR 350 crore potential revenue from FY28
items.quote: Approximately INR3,700 crores, yes, more or less, give or take, INR50 crores at today's price.

items.statement: Working capital days improved from 17 to 12 days; receivables and inventory reduced; Somany Max JV loss narrowed from INR 7 cr to ~INR 1 cr YoY
items.quote: Working capital days also have come down from 17 to 12 days.

items.statement: Targeting >15% YoY top-line growth to ~INR1,350 cr in FY27
items.quote: We are targeting a top line growth of more than 15% year-on-year, resulting into about INR1,350 crores for this financial year, maintaining a healthy bottom line.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target ~INR1,600 cr (+/- INR50 cr)
items.quote: Next year, you're looking at about INR1,600 crores plus/minus INR50 crores.

items.statement: Standalone order book INR2,156 cr (66% defense, 34% space/met/hydro) as of Q1 FY27 end
items.quote: Our stand-alone order book as of quarter end stands at INR2,156 crores, providing strong visibility for the upcoming period. Around 66% of this order book is from defense and the rest that is 34% is from space, metrology and hydrology sectors.

items.statement: Consolidated order book INR2,849 cr including INR244 cr service orders
items.quote: Our consolidated order book stands at INR2,849 crores, which includes service orders of about INR244 crores, which are typically more accretive to margins.

items.statement: Secured INR2,205 cr order from HAL for Uttam Radar subsystems in July 2026
items.quote: In the month of July, we secured a significant order worth about INR2,205 crores from Hindustan Aeronautics Limited for procurement of critical subsystems for Uttam Radar.

items.statement: Total order book ~INR4,300 cr as on date after HAL order
items.quote: So with this major win, our total order book sells to a record-breaking of INR4,300 crores as on date.

items.statement: Expect INR1,600 cr new order inflows in FY27 (excl. HAL order)
items.quote: M.V.R. confirms that we will see at least INR1,600 crores being added this year. And we may improve that number by the way, over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Order intake visibility INR8,000-9,000 cr over next 3-4 years for execution over 5-6 years
items.quote: Our order intake over the next 3 to 4 years, I think should be in the region of at least INR8,000 crores to INR9,000 crores to be executed over the next 5 to 6 years.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected similar to FY26 with positive delta
items.quote: Definitely, definitely, the margins are going to be similar to last year. You can expect a delta increase on that -- positive increase in that margins.

items.statement: Invested in automated process engineering workflows and advanced infrastructure for large-scale execution
items.quote: To support this rapidly growing volume and complexity of work, we have invested steadily in automated process engineering workflows and advanced infrastructure.

items.statement: Space & Weather division to be spun off as separate listed entity effective April 1, 2027
items.quote: The company shall operate as an independent entity from April 1, 2027, is our expectation.

items.statement: Supply chain stretch risk highlighted; beefing up purchase dept to mitigate
items.quote: So we've got to make sure that our supply chains remain intact and stuff comes in within the defined time lines.

items.statement: Sustained government focus on meteorological budgets expected due to climate change
items.quote: So given all these things combined, I think there should be and there ought to be and from indications are, there will be a sustained focus on meteorological budgets.

items.statement: Revised FY27 revenue guidance to INR 2,200-2,300 crore with EBITDA margin of 10-11% (INR 220-230 crore EBITDA), down from prior INR 2,000-2,400 crore revenue and INR 250-280 crore EBITDA guidance.
items.quote: So basically, what we are guiding is INR2,200 crores to INR2,300 crores top line and EBITDA margin in the range of 10% to 11%. So, it will be in that range between INR220 crores, INR230 crores kind of EBITDA.

items.statement: Expects normalized EBITDA margins of 12-14% in FY28 once raw material pressures ease and capacity utilization improves.
items.quote: In fiscal '28, I think it's in the region of 12% to 14% is what we can look at.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin collapsed to 4% from 45% in Q4 FY26 due to raw material cost spikes, freight increases, and inability to fully pass on costs.
items.quote: You would have seen the details of our financial statements and you would have seen that our margins, which were plus 45% last quarter, has come down to 4%, and that's what has percolated down to our EBITDA for the quarter.

items.statement: Specialty Ingredients segment EBITDA margin was 6.35% in Q1 FY27; expects improvement to >10% normalized as raw material costs stabilize and price pass-through improves.
items.quote: The EBITDA is 6.35% here. Predominantly, it has come down basically because of raw material prices being high.

items.statement: Aroma (vanillin) segment EBITDA negative INR 4-4.5 crore in Q1 FY27 due to low capacity utilization (25%) during ethyl vanillin ramp-up; expects positive EBITDA in Q2 FY27 and 7% EBITDA margin at $13/kg pricing with 3,000 tons annual volume
items.quote: As the capacity utilization crosses 70%, 80% in the subsequent quarters, we will absorb almost all the fixed costs. And on a yearly basis, it's come down to that. This is a cutoff in a quarter where the expenditures are for the full capacity, but the utilization is hardly 25%.

items.statement: Revised FY27 vanillin production guidance down to ~3,000 tons from 3,600-4,000 tons due to slower ethyl vanillin ramp-up and 4 campaign changeovers costing ~4 months production time.
items.quote: So basically, we had guided for 3,600 to 4,000 and now we are saying 3,000 -- around 3,000. The change is basically in our ethyl vanillin run. The ramp-up we took was slower than what we had anticipated purely because we wanted to get the quality standards to be absolutely undoubtable.

items.statement: Raw material cost pressures persist due to geopolitical conflict (Red Sea/Hormuz Strait); expects elevated prices for at least 3 months; able to pass on ~50% of cost increases in blends in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: In Q2, it will remain with us because I don't see so much of a difference in raw material prices because with the war situation and the conflict, it keeps moving in directions which we don't understand sometimes.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced to INR 640 crore from INR 670 crore (Mar 2026); may need INR 100-200 crore additional credit lines in FY27 for working capital; targeting to secure lines in 1-1.5 months.
items.quote: We will try to use the internal cash, but it looks like as the year progresses, we may have to go and go and take credit lines from the market in the range of INR100 crores to INR200 crores plus.

items.statement: Working capital cycle elongated to ~100 days due to Red Sea shipping rerouting and slower customer collections; using supplier/dealer financing which adds 1-1.5% to raw material costs.
items.quote: Working capital remains a bit of a concern because of the elongated working capital cycles. As you know, with the Hormuz Strait and the Red Sea issues, we have to now ship it across the South Africa, and that has increased the working capital needs.

items.statement: Vanillin channel inventories cleared globally; U.S./Europe demand gap of 5,000-6,000 tons identified due to antidumping duties; demand pickup confirmed with F&F majors for quarterly/annual contracts.
items.quote: Those are dried out. There is no overhang of any channel stock, either Chinese or pre antidumping duty on now. So, there is no channel stocks in any of the country.

items.statement: CFS Europe liquidated (no further cash burn); China entity liquidation underway with INR 10-20 crore expenditure in Q2 FY27; Brazil fire insurance claim settled at INR 400 crore with 20% haircut.
items.quote: China is in the process of liquidation. We have been telling it that this will happen this year, and we will have around INR10 million to INR20 million of expenditure, which we'll be incurring during this quarter.

items.statement: Expect positive sales growth from Q2 FY27 as monsoon improves and agriculture activity normalizes
items.quote: Difficult to give the number, but we should be positive and that positive impact should be visible from Q2 itself, I believe.

items.statement: Target to double company size in 4-5 years through product mix, technical manufacturing and international business
items.quote: The idea is to double ourselves. In the past, we used to double in 3 to 4 years. Now I believe that we should be able to double in 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Sotanala project total investment ~INR200 crores (INR50 crores formulation, INR150 crores technical), INR70 crores spent so far
items.quote: It will be a project total investment. These total investment will go roughly about INR200 crores, out of which I think about INR50 crores will be going in the formulations and INR150 crores will be for the technical. And the total investment made so far is to the tune of about INR70 crores.

items.statement: Annual capex to normalize to INR30-40 crores maintenance after current investment cycle ends
items.quote: Once the current projects are completed, we expect annual capex to normalize around INR30 crores to INR40 crores of maintenance capex, allowing us to increasingly focus on utilization, cash generation and returns.

items.statement: Target to increase premium product contribution to 70% of B2C sales in next 3-4 years
items.quote: five years back when we started this exercise when the contribution from the premium product was 48%. Now we have reached to 60-plus percentage already and the target is to reach to 70% in next three years to four years time.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 240bps to 31.6% in Q1 FY27 despite 12% revenue decline, driven by premium mix and 2% price increase
items.quote: I just told actually that there was a 13% decline in the volume and there was 2% rise in the prices. So, this price rise can be due to the focus on the specialty products and some advantage due to inventory also you can say

items.statement: Sales returns expected but reduced to at least half of prior year's INR200 crores due to cautious placement strategy
items.quote: I think that we should be able to reduce the sales return numbers to at least half what was there in the previous year.

items.statement: Crude/petroleum-linked raw material costs pressured margins; calibrated pricing, better mix and differentiated products used to offset
items.quote: On the operating side, crude and petroleum-linked raw material costs remain an area of pressure during the quarter, impacting parts of crop protection value chain. We continue to address this through calibrated pricing, better product mix and increasing contribution from the differentiated products while remaining comp

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance maintained at minimum 50% for FY27
items.quote: So I think revenue guidance remains the same. It will be at least 50%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to be maintained despite aggressive store expansion
items.quote: And we will try to maintain the EBITDA margins even after opening so much new area.

items.statement: SSSG guidance for FY27 at 8-10%
items.quote: And the guidance for SSSG has always been 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Per store capex increased 10% to INR 1.2-1.22 crores from INR 1.1 crores
items.quote: So earlier, the capex used to be about INR1.1 crores. So I think it is up because of the prices rising, it has moved up to INR1.2 crores, INR1.22 crores.

items.statement: On track to open 170-200 stores in FY27, 56 net stores added in Q1
items.quote: Yes, we are on track to open 170 to 200 stores this year.

items.statement: 4-5% garment cost increase from Q3 FY27 due to raw material inflation, to be passed to consumers
items.quote: So I think we'll start seeing that impact from the third quarter onwards, and it will be an increase of about, I would say, 4% to 5% increase in the overall garment cost, which we'll have to pass on to the consumer.

items.statement: Demand inelastic in value fashion; kids wear 25% of sales ensures recurring need
items.quote: We think we are selling necessity to the consumers. And for example, kids wear is 25% of our sales. So you have to buy new clothes for your kids every year.

items.statement: Full price sales 90% in Q1 (down from 92% due to Adhik Maas), volume growth 56%
items.quote: Full price sales contributed approximately 90% of sales in the first quarter, reflecting healthy demand and disciplined inventory management.

items.statement: Geopolitical tension led to higher safety stock; targeting inventory 90-100 days, creditors 45-50 days
items.quote: Lastly, due to geopolitical tension, we have increased our safety stock in the warehouse for seamless availability of stock, which has resulted in higher inventory levels.

items.statement: New stores at INR 730-740/sq ft vs mature stores at INR 1,070-1,100/sq ft; 10-12 stores below INR 600/sq ft
items.quote: So the new stores per square feet sale is about 34% less than our mature stores. So more than 2 years old stores are already performing at a very high level of almost INR1,070 to INR1,100 per square feet of sale.

items.statement: Repeat customer rate improved from 40% to 55% over 3 years; NPS tracking and AI queue management implemented
items.quote: So in fact, in the last 3 years, people who came back to us within the first year has moved up from 40% to almost 55%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 16-18% by year-end FY27
items.quote: On our EBITDA margins, I should say that even if things go along the way they are, we should be reaching closer to about at least between 16% to 18% by the year-end.

items.statement: PM3 major rebuild underway, commissioning within a week; major capex cycle complete
items.quote: With the commissioning of our last machine on our upgradation program, which is our PM3 that is going to be coming on stream within this month in about a week or so.

items.statement: Peak debt at INR 760-770 cr; repayment of INR 170-175 cr/year for 2-3 years to reach <INR 300 cr
items.quote: Peak debt, we are currently looking at about INR760 crores or INR770 crores maximum. And we have repayments of about INR170 crores, INR175 crores for the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 13.2%; cost increase of INR 4,200/ton offset NSR gain of INR 3,400/ton QoQ
items.quote: However, the improvement in blended NSR by approximately INR3,400 per ton was more than offset by an increase in cost of around INR4,200 per ton on a quarter-to-quarter basis.

items.statement: Demand supportive; dealer inventory minimal, pipelines empty suggesting demand surge
items.quote: Pipelines are relatively empty and which suggests that there is likely going to be a surge towards a surge of demand in paper and which is likely to impact our pricing also positively.

items.statement: Specialty paper share at 18-19% of revenue; target 30%; OGR paper commercialized on PM2
items.quote: Right now, our contribution from specialty paper is just under 20%. It's about 18%, 19%, but we will surely be making our efforts to reach that level of 30%.

items.statement: West Asia conflict driving 50% of cost increase; local wheat straw prices elevated but cooling
items.quote: So I would say about 50-odd percent of the increased cost is due to the West Asia crisis. Rest of it is more local depending on the state in which we are operating.

items.statement: AI integration in manufacturing targeting 4-5% cost reduction by March 2028
items.quote: We could target between 4% to 5% additions in -- or reductions in costs.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty application filed for writing/printing paper (40-140 GSM); decision awaited
items.quote: We have already done that. We are already in close coordination with the government, where our applications for antidumping duty and anti-subsidy duty has already been filed.

items.statement: Pulp capacity to increase to 410-415 TPD from 365 TPD to support full paper capacity
items.quote: So pulp capacity should -- will increase to about 410, 415 tons per day, and that's all that we will require to produce the relevant quantities of paper.

items.statement: Imported copier/Maplitho paper priced at $610-620/ton at port; volumes not significant
items.quote: So imported price, we are currently seeing trending between $610 and $620 per ton. Volumes are not large enough to create any kind of negative impact.

items.statement: No volume guidance for DI pipes and ferroalloys for FY27 due to uncertainty in government ordering and state-level fund releases
items.quote: For giving any numbers, I think it will be speculative right now because there are a lot of moving parts. Different states are giving -- some of the states have started giving orders, some of the states have still problems. So, it has not opened up entirely for pan -India. So, it will be very difficult for us to give y

items.statement: Ferroalloy capacity utilization expected at 80-90% after new module commissioning by Dec-Jan
items.quote: In ferroalloys, we achieved a capacity utilization of more than 80% in the last quarter, and it is around 27% of the turnover currently. So, as we commission the new module by December -January, capacity utilization in ferroalloys will remain at around 80% to 90%.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR7,000-7,500 crores with current capacity in a normal market by FY28
items.quote: Sir, with the given capacity probably which is getting completed in Q3 of this year, you can say end of the calendar year December 2026, with the given capacity it should reach INR7,000 crores to INR7,500 crores in a normal market.

items.statement: Total project outlay revised to INR1,112 crores from INR1,000 crores; INR1,076 crores already invested; balance INR35-40 crores by end of 2026
items.quote: We have already invested INR1,076 crores, mostly through internal accruals, while the overall project outlay has been revised from around INR1,000 crores to INR1,112 crores, primarily due to technical upgrades, additional ancillaries, some inflation, and some time overruns also. The balance of around INR35 crores to IN

items.statement: DI pipe order book equivalent to ~4 months of current dispatch capacity
items.quote: Madam, as per the current dispatch position, it is the equivalent of say , the current capacity utilization, it is around four months' order book.

items.statement: Specialized ferroalloy margins 15-18% vs conventional steel 5-7%; long-term sustainable range 15-20%
items.quote: See, for ferroalloy business, as the share of specialty ferroalloy increase in our overall mix, we expect the margin to sustain between 15% to 20%.

items.statement: DI pipe margins currently at rock bottom (~12% in Q1); could improve to 18% if prices recover
items.quote: Whatever we have achieved in first quarter around 12%, that is good enough and it should go up to 18% if the prices improve. One thing which I also mentioned, I think you might have missed it also, is that today we are sitting at the rock bottom prices. From here the prices cannot be worse. Demand cannot be worse. It h

items.statement: Post-monsoon recovery expected in DI pipe dispatches and payments from Q3 FY27 as Jal Jeevan Mission funds release improves
items.quote: Recently in this year, already around INR10,344 crores have been released by the center and gradually the matching share will be also given by the different states. So, we would be looking at a post -monsoon recovery in the dispatches and the payments, and from the third quarter things should improve now.

items.statement: DI pipe demand recovery dependent on government fund releases and contractor payments; competitive intensity high until utilization crosses 65-70%
items.quote: See, the competitive intensity will be there because currently because the currently the industry with our pipe capacity utilization this particular quarter was only 30% on the enhanced capacity. Similarly, competitors, they also are operating somebody in 25% range, somebody in 30%, 35% range. So, competition intensity

items.statement: Net term debt reduced to INR188 crores in Q1 FY27 from INR3,408 crores in FY21; debt-equity ratio 0.07; working capital sanctioned limit INR550 crores, net utilization below INR500 crores
items.quote: We have also continued to make strong progress on deleveraging with our net term debt reducing significantly from INR3,408 crores in FY21 to INR188 crores in Q1 FY27. Our net term debt to debt-equity ratio stands at a healthy 0.07 in FY26 end, providing us with a strong financial foundation and ample headroom to suppor

items.statement: DI pipe capacity utilization at 30% in Q1 (41,000 tons); target 50-60% as orders improve; management hopes for >60% when demand normalizes
items.quote: Right now, in the first quarter, the capacity utilization was 30% of the enhanced capacity. Around 100 and going forward as per the orders improve, we are ready to encash this. Production in the first quarter was 41,000. The annual capacity is 5,50,000. It is somewhere in the range of 30%, 33%. And if the market improv

items.statement: TMT bar sales in West Bengal expected to rise from 15-20% to 50-70% of production due to increased state development activity
items.quote: So, these products in Bengal, we were selling hardly 15%, 20% of our material. Going forward in the next year, we are foreseeing that probably we'll be able to sell around 50% to 60%, 70% of our TMT bars in West Bengal.

items.statement: RetailerShakti EBITDA expected to turn positive in Q3 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA number we are closer to break even and expect to make positive EBITDA in Q3 this financial year end.

items.statement: JITO private label gross margin above 50%; Q1 FY27 revenue INR79 lakh vs INR25 lakh in Q4 FY26
items.quote: And the gross margin is above 50%. So this Jito revenue ramp up will increase the gross margin.

items.statement: Existing fulfilment infrastructure can support 100% growth to INR2,500-3,000 cr annual revenue; new warehouses under construction in Guwahati, Udaipur, Patna, Lucknow
items.quote: Our existing warehouse infrastructure or fulfilment center infrastructure are ready to take up around 100% growth from the current level. So INR2500 crores to INR3000 crores it means next year 2028 we don't have any issue for the existing infrastructure.

items.statement: RetailerShakti grew 48% YoY; SastaSundar grew 44% YoY; 67% RetailerShakti and 78% SastaSundar revenue from tier 2/3 markets
items.quote: RetailerShakti grew 48% Y-o-Y, continuing to remain our principal growth engine. While SastaSundar grew 44% Y-o-Y, reflecting a strong B2C business.

items.statement: JITO private label scaling: 19 Health Buddies converted, 25 in pipeline; target 50% conversion in 3 months; new pure-play JITO franchise channel launched
items.quote: We have already converted 19 Healthbuddies into JITO and 25 are in pipeline. So around 50% of the Healthbuddy will be converted into JITO in next 3 months time.

items.statement: EBITDA not a priority for next 2-3 years; focus on cash flow and capital efficiency; SastaSundar burn ~15% of revenue for customer acquisition and tech
items.quote: We are not an EBITDA positive company for the next two, three years and we neither look the EBITDA from perspective. So EBITDA is not our priority, our priority is building a very, very large company without looking hurriedly EBITDA in SastaSundar business.

items.statement: AI-monitored RetailAir SaaS for retailers scheduled to launch next quarter; aims to reduce retailer inventory from 30 days to 5-6 days
items.quote: We are continuously working to launch our AI-monitored RetailAir product for our retailers, and we are scheduled to launch in this quarter. Hopefully in the next quarter we will confirm the success of the project.

items.statement: SEBI approval for merger/demerger scheme on track; responding to stock exchange queries
items.quote: Yes, yes, we are absolutely on track. We have started taking questions from stock exchange and replying them. We don't find any problem into anything so far.

items.statement: Capex plan: rent-first model for immediate capacity, then build owned warehouses; Guwahati 75,000 sq ft construction starting in 6 months; Udaipur construction started; Patna, Lucknow in 2-3 months
items.quote: We take on rent and start immediately warehousing, and in the meantime, wherever is we see the good potentiality, we start building large capacity side by side, so that we can shift for the next growth phase.

items.statement: SastaSundar burn split: 25-30% marketing/branding, 40-45% tech/AI, 30% sales team/geographic expansion
items.quote: Breakup of this burning is somewhere around 25% to 30% is towards marketing and advertisement, while the 40% to 45% goes towards tech related cost.

items.statement: West Bengal market share ~3-4%; target to double to 7% in 2-3 years; Northeast highest growth region; Jharkhand warehouse planned in Ranchi
items.quote: Current market share in Kolkata and West Bengal should be around 3%, 4%. In next two, three years we want to make it double from here, so say 7%.

items.statement: Management reiterated prior FY27 guidance without providing new numbers
items.quote: So I would just say one thing that as we have given the guidance earlier, we are on it, and we will be proving our best out of the business what we are currently doing.

items.statement: No major capex planned for FY27 beyond INR 5-10 crore maintenance capex
items.quote: for this particular financial year, we are not planning for any additional capex, except a small operational capex to the extent of INR 5 crores to INR 10 crores.

items.statement: Targeting 10-12% consolidated EBITDA margin within 1-2 quarters
items.quote: If you ask me about, again, aspiration, I want to go this quarter. But realistically, yes, we may take 1 or 2 quarters more to reach up to that level.

items.statement: Jumbo laminate capacity utilization target 55-60% in FY27, 70-75% next year
items.quote: our next aspiration about using this plant at 50%, 55% this year, and we will be utilizing like 70%, 75% next year.

items.statement: Jumbo laminate revenue potential INR 75 crore at 60% utilization, INR 140 crore at 90%
items.quote: this year, our aspiration, again, is to take it to somewhere around 60% of utilization, which will take us to somewhere around INR 75 crores. And going ahead, if we utilize the capacity at somewhere around 90%, the potential revenue we can generate from this press would be somewhere around INR 140 crores.

items.statement: Jumbo laminate EBITDA margin 20.6% in Q1 FY27, expected to be maintained
items.quote: we would say our expectation is we would maintain such margins across the year.

items.statement: Resin prices up 35-40% QoQ, wood prices flat; only marginal correction in July
items.quote: Wood pricing has remained flat this quarter, but the resin prices have gone substantially high like somewhere around close to 35% to 40%.

items.statement: MDF 15% price hike sustained, no further hikes expected as market won't accept
items.quote: No. So currently, the 15% hike is what we are sustaining at. And we are not passing any kind of discounts or anything. So we are maintaining our given price hike.

items.statement: Laminate 10% price hike covering inflation, no further hikes expected
items.quote: In laminate, the 10% price is covering our inflation as of now. And we don't see a further hike in that as well.

items.statement: MDF industry growing at 20% CAGR, can absorb 800 CBM/day additional capacity
items.quote: MDF as an industry is growing at a 20% CAGR. And when we talk about 20% CAGR, that means an additional capacity of 800 cubic meters a day can be absorbed in the market easily.

items.statement: High freight costs and container shortages limiting MDF exports; West Asia conflict disrupting shipping
items.quote: freight costs were significantly higher and the shipping routes continue to face disruption arising from ongoing conflict in West Asia.

items.statement: Debt at INR 260 crore including working capital; repaying INR 55 crore annually; targeting debt-free by FY29
items.quote: As of now, if you see the debt, including working capital is around INR 260 crores. Now we have got a scheduled repayment. And as per the schedule, every year, we are making a repayment of almost INR 55 crores.

items.statement: MDF value-added target 50% volume, 60% revenue; Q1 FY27 at 45% volume, 54% revenue
items.quote: internally, we have a target of MDF per se to achieve the, I mean, quantity-wise target of 50% and value-wise 60% in terms of products.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue target INR 16,000-17,000 crore; FY28 INR 21,000 crore; FY29 INR 24,000-25,000 crore
items.quote: Precisely, INR 16,000 to 17,000 crore.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated PAT target INR 1,100-1,200 crore; FY28 INR 1,300-1,400 crore; FY29 INR 2,000 crore
items.quote: And the PAT will be around INR 1,100 to 1,200, during this year. Next year, INR 1,300 to 1,400, and, of course, FY29 around INR 2,000 CR, we are expecting a PAT.

items.statement: Standalone FY27 revenue target INR 13,000-14,000 crore
items.quote: Around INR 13,000 to 14,000 crores on standalone.

items.statement: Expects PAT margin 6-6.5% and EBITDA margin 6.5-7% minimum going forward
items.quote: 6-6.5% PAT, and the EBITDA, 6.5-7% minimum.

items.statement: Standalone order book INR 1,12,000 crore; consolidated INR 1,27,000 crore (60% redevelopment, 40% PMC)
items.quote: NBCC's standalone order book stands INR 1,12,000 crores and consolidated order book INR 1,27,000 crores.

items.statement: Expects INR 50,000-60,000 crore new orders in FY27 including 5 GPRA (~INR 30,000 crore) and 2-3 other big orders
items.quote: Total. Only GPRA around INR 30,000 crores we may get. Apart from GPRA, we are expecting two, three big orders. So that altogether, INR 50,000 to 60,000 crores we are expecting.

items.statement: Awarded INR 1,700 crore tenders in Q1; expects INR 18,000-20,000 crore new works awarded in next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: In the next 2-3 quarters, we are expecting INR 18,000 to 20,000 CR new works will be awarded.

items.statement: CPSE REIT: Board approved SPV formation; will transfer 75,000 sq ft rentable assets; partnering with MTNL, BSNL, ITI etc. for national REIT
items.quote: The Board has accorded in principle approval for incorporation of wholly owned subsidiary as an SPV for the proposed CPSE REIT, subject to approval of administrative ministry and DIPAM.

items.statement: Cash balance INR 666 crore as of 30 June 2026
items.quote: Cash is INR 666 crore as on 30th June.

items.statement: FY27 disbursement target Rs 5,000 Cr; AUM growth 13-14%; reduce gross NPA by Rs 40 Cr to below 2% by Mar-27
items.quote: In respect of guidance, I stick on a guidance of what I have given in my last concall that is Rs.5000 Crores disbursements and 13 % to 14% growth in the AUM and reducing NPA by Rs.40 Crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 disbursement target Rs 1,200-1,250 Cr; aim to bring June NPA of Rs 427 Cr down to March level of ~Rs 405 Cr by Sep-26
items.quote: For current quarter, we are targeting Rs.1,200 Crores to Rs.1,250 Crores disbursements and we set a target to bring down June NPA to last March NPA level.

items.statement: Spread may compress by 10-12 bps next quarter due to aggressive pricing to drive disbursements and retain customers; NHB refinance and bank renegotiation to keep cost of funds stable
items.quote: So ultimately, my spread may, going forward, may come down by 10 to 12, maximum of 10 basis points in next coming quarter.

items.statement: NHB sanctioned Rs 600 Cr refinance; Rs 106 Cr already availed in early Aug; remainder to be drawn as needed; borrowing mix 86% banks, 6.2% NHB, 4.8% Repco Bank, 1% NCD, 0.5% CP/PTC
items.quote: During the current financial year, we have received a refinance support from National Housing Bank to the extent of Rs.600 Crores. Out of Rs.600 Crores, we already availed Rs.106 Crores during the first week of August.

items.statement: AUM Rs 15,990 Cr as of Jun-26 (excl. unrealised cheques), up 8.9% YoY; sanctions Rs 938 Cr, disbursements Rs 843 Cr in Q1 FY27
items.quote: AUM stands at Rs.15,990 Crores as end of June 30, 2026. We have seen 8.9% year-on-year growth in the AUM.

items.statement: Gross NPA Rs 427 Cr (2.7%) vs Rs 405 Cr (2.6%) QoQ; down from Rs 485 Cr (YoY); Stage 2 at 7.2% vs 7% QoQ, 9.7% YoY; PCR 54%; recoveries ongoing but insufficient to upgrade accounts
items.quote: As end of the June, our GNPA in absolute terms, stood at Rs.427 Crores with the GNPA ratio of 2.7% compared to Rs.405 Crores and 2.6% in the previous quarter of the same period.

items.statement: Focus on non-Tamil Nadu states (AP, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP) for growth; Tamil Nadu already strong at 57% of book
items.quote: This year, starting, we have started concentrating on non-TN states. To start with the southern non-TN states like Andhra, Telangana, and Karnataka, we want to do good.

items.statement: Solar EPC order book of 1,500 pumps won in first 4 months of FY27; 800 executed, 700 pending to be completed by July-end
items.quote: During this quarter, we had two important order wins in the Solar EPC business. First, we had received an order for 500 solar pumps from M SEDCL and again, in July, last month also, we got another order for 1000 pumps. So all in all, for the first 4 months, we have a total order of 1500 pumps.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved 99 bps YoY to 12.07% despite raw material cost headwinds
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter increased 26.7% to Rs. 9.86 crores and our EBITDA margin also improved by 99 basis points to 12.07%.

items.statement: Polymer prices (LLDPE/HDPE) up 30-35% vs Jan-Feb; free-market prices already passed on; Gujarat subsidy prices revised, other states by end Q2, central mechanism by Sep-end
items.quote: So just at the end of March, because of the geopolitical situation, the prices of key raw materials, which is L LDP and HDP E, that increased by 50%. But after that, the prices have stabilized. So right now, they would be up around 30%-35% compared to what it was in January or February period.

items.statement: Full benefit of price revisions expected from Q3 FY27 as state and central subsidy price corrections complete by end Q2
items.quote: So definitely from Q3, we can see the full impact of that price revision. And additionally, the central government has also constituted price revision mechanism. So that also we are expecting by end of September.

items.statement: Ahmedabad facility (70,000 sq ft) commenced production; targets in-house manufacturing of valves, connectors, accessories (10% of system value); full ramp-up in 2-3 years
items.quote: Another important milestone during the quarter was the commencement of our production facility spread across 70,000 square feet near Ahmedabad in Gujarat. So this facility strengthens our manufacturing capacity in micro -irrigation business and enables production of critical components and accessories.

items.statement: Solar EPC segment targeted to reach 50% of overall business in next 3 years; expansion beyond Maharashtra to Rajasthan, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Haryana
items.quote: So definitely, it will be an important part of our growth and we are expecting that the overall contribution for solar EPC segment would reach 50% over next 3 years.

items.statement: Current micro-irrigation manufacturing capacity (Rajkot, Kurnool, Ahmedabad) sufficient for ~Rs 600 cr revenue; no manufacturing bottleneck; solar EPC growth constrained only by execution capacity
items.quote: So with the existing manufacturing capacity for micro-irrigation business that we have at Rajkot, at Kurnool, and also now with Ahmedabad plant, we can comfortably target micro -irrigation business of around Rs. 600 crores.

items.statement: Solar pump empanelment discussions advanced in new states; tenders expected to float in September for Rajasthan, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Haryana
items.quote: So we are awaiting tender release from these states and majority of states are indicating that they would be floating in September.

items.statement: 60-70% of solar rooftop business sourced from existing 750 micro-irrigation dealers; solar pumps use dedicated dealer network
items.quote: So for the solar rooftop business, I can say that majority of our rooftop business is coming from the existing dealer network. So almost 60%-70% of solar rooftop business is coming from the existing micro-irrigation dealers.

items.statement: FY27 priorities: ramp Ahmedabad facility, expand solar EPC order book, improve micro-irrigation revenue mix (commercial/non-subsidy/allied products), disciplined execution, working capital management
items.quote: As we look ahead, our priorities for FY ' 27 remain clear , r amping up the Ahmedabad manufacturing facility, expanding our solar EPC order book and for the micro -irrigation business, improving our revenue mix.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue growth target maintained at 18% despite Q1 export deferrals
items.quote: We continue to believe that we'll be able to achieve the target which we have given.

items.statement: Laminate revenue growth guided at 10-12% for FY27
items.quote: We still maintain that we will be able to grow in that range.

items.statement: FY27 capex budgeted at INR130-135 crores including INR70 crores for laminate press lines
items.quote: Our capex for the year is budgeted around INR130 crores, INR135 crores, which includes INR70 crores towards the laminate expansion.

items.statement: INR27 crores of export shipments postponed from Q1 to Q2 due to container/vessel delays
items.quote: Nearly INR27 crores of export shipment got postponed out of this quarter.

items.statement: Chipboard EBITDA margin target 18-20% at full capacity utilization with better product mix
items.quote: On a full capacity utilization on a better product mix, it can achieve a margin of 18%, 20%.

items.statement: Laminate EBITDA margin historically around 15-16%
items.quote: In the past, we have already stated that laminate can grow at around 15%, 16% of the margin.

items.statement: Net 7-8% price hikes passed on in laminates and chipboard due to chemical cost inflation
items.quote: Overall, on a net basis, we have passed on 7% to 8% of the price hikes.

items.statement: West Asia conflict causing freight cost volatility, container delays, and chemical price fluctuations
items.quote: The ongoing West Asia conflicts continue to keep input prices, currency rates and freight costs volatile during this quarter.

items.statement: Net debt reduction of ~INR100 crores targeted in FY27 despite capex; accelerated repayment from FY28
items.quote: We expect that it should come down by close to around INR100-odd crores.

items.statement: Plywood segment EBITDA breakeven targeted for FY27; PAT breakeven timeline uncertain
items.quote: We are very hopeful that in this year, we will do the EBITDA breakeven.

items.statement: Aspire to operate 12 outdoor parks by 2030, adding ~1 park per year; indoor Hello Park centers are additional
items.quote: By 2030, we aspire to operate a portfolio of 12 parks, having kept targets of adding approximately one park every year.

items.statement: INR 50 crore invested for 50.002% stake in Mehsana Next Parks (Shanku's Water Park)
items.quote: The company has announced an investment of INR50 crores for a 50.002% stake in Mehsana Next Parks Private Limited, the SPV that owns and operates Shanku's Water Park.

items.statement: Hello Park indoor centers capex INR 8-12 crore each; target 2-3 centers per year
items.quote: The capital investment per center is expected to be INR8 to INR12 crores, making it an efficient capitalized fast-growth format.
