Shah Commerce. So that spending has also been expensed in the quarter. So most of the last three, four quarters, we have been setting up the st

items.statement: Commerce demerger on track; NCLT hearing scheduled 17 Aug 2026; expect completion by mid-Sep 2026
items.quote: The next NCLT hearing is scheduled in Chennai on 17th August, which is coming Monday, and we expect the entire process to be completed by possibly the first half of September 2026, which is next month.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin ~36%; Commerce segment EBITDA margin ~40%; Academic segment EBITDA margin ~75%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter came in at INR54 crores, registering 10% year -on-year growth, reflecting an EBITDA marg in of approximately 36% and continued disciplined cost management.

items.statement: Offline commerce EBITDA margin ~35%; Online commerce EBITDA margin 45-48%
items.quote: Offline margins, we stood at peak at 35 percentage whereas our online sits at 45 to 48 percentage.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 enrollments up 35% YoY to 1.03 lakh; collections up 27% YoY to INR165 cr
items.quote: Overall enrollments during the quarter grew 35% year -on-year to about 1.03 lakh students, while collections grew 27% year -on-year, reflecting a healthy demand and robust execution across all our business segments.

items.statement: Commerce offline:online revenue split ~330:120 cr (FY27 target); expanding into Class 11-12 digital (Commerce Virtuals) and CMA India
items.quote: We expect the offline, online split to be about like our offline sales are at almost INR 330 crores and the offline at -- online is INR120 crores . So we are a major into off -line split with a hybrid brick -and-mortar model.

items.statement: Debt cost reduced to 9-9.5% from 17.5%; quarterly finance cost sustainable at INR7.5-8 cr
items.quote: So currently, the debt is at a cost of about 9% to 9.5%, bringing it down from a 17.5%, which we had last year.

items.statement: No deferred consideration payouts for next 12-15 months; structured payouts from FY28 over 5-7 years
items.quote: There are no -- there are no deferred consideration payouts for next one year. So we are having the structured payouts in the next FY28 coming in the next five years, six and seven years.

items.statement: Government test prep targets INR100 cr EBITDA in 4-5 years; expanding into Karnataka and defense exam prep
items.quote: We continue to build strongly on the other two verticals, which is in our government test prep, where we expect and working towards reaching INR100 crores of EBITDA over the next four to five years.

items.statement: K-12 managed schools: 6 schools, 5,400 students; targeting expansion with steady occupancy and fee growth
items.quote: We currently manage six schools with over 5,400 students on an asset -light end -to-end managed services model and are targeting to expand the number of schools that we manage, supported by steady occupancy and fee growth dynamics in the coming years.

items.statement: SNVA Veranda stake held in non-commerce entity; expect value unlocking from that investment
items.quote: The shareholding in SNVA will be sitting in the Veranda non -commerce entity. So that value will accrue into the non -commerce.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance maintained at around 20% for FY27
items.quote: And yes, we are maintaining the guidance at similar level.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 18% over next 2 years, FY27 margin expected below 17%
items.quote: See, the intent is to take it to 18% in coming 2 years to go. But definitely for FY27, it should be less than 17% on an overall basis.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR100-110 crores for FY27, primarily INR70 crores for spooling facility
items.quote: Around INR100-odd crores, we are targeting new capex and net debt is INR325-odd crores as on June 30.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR600 crores plus INR185 crores LOI for spooling, total near INR800 crores
items.quote: Our order book for the quarter also stood strong at more than INR600 crores without considering the LOI of INR185 crores with a strong mix of domestic and export reflecting strong demand for our products.

items.statement: EBITDA margin stable at 16.1% in Q1 FY27, target 18% in 2 years driven by fittings and spooling
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 16.1%, broadly stable compared to 16.2% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Fittings expected to contribute 5-7% of revenue in FY27, 8-10% in FY28; spooling 5% in FY27, 10-15% in FY28
items.quote: FY27, we are expecting around 5% to 7% of the total top line and coming year to go, we are expecting around 10% something between 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Strong demand from power, engineering, chemical, oil & gas; data center capacity targeting 8x growth to 10.5 GW in 5 years
items.quote: India data center capacity, what we believe was around 1.3 gigawatt roughly in 2025, which is targeting to grow by 8x around 10.5 gigawatt in coming 5 years.

items.statement: Revenue growth driven by volume growth and higher realizations from steel price increases; EBITDA per kg improved
items.quote: Revenue growth was driven by a combination of volume growth and higher realization. With realization benefiting from the increase in steel prices, while higher steel prices supported reported revenues, our EBITDA per kg also improved.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions creating export uncertainty; EU safeguard quota reduced 25% but impact minimal due to diversified geographies
items.quote: However, the prevailing geopolitical tensions have created some uncertainty in the export environment.

items.statement: Spooling facility on track to commence by end of Q3 FY27 (December 2026), asset turnover expected >3x
items.quote: The project is progressing well, and we remain on track to commence the spooling facility by end of this year.

items.statement: Volume growth >7% YoY in Q1 FY27; targeting >15% volume growth for FY27 alongside 20% revenue growth
items.quote: No, if I take fittings, spooling, seamless, welded altogether, we believe we should be higher than 15% on the volume front also.

items.statement: Net debt at INR325 crores as of June 30, 2026; utilization at 60% welded, 85-90% seamless
items.quote: Primarily net debt level, it is around INR325-odd crores(incorrectly pronounced as 280 crores).

items.statement: Consolidated sales growth expected at low-to-mid teens for FY27; India Engineering at mid-to-high teens
items.quote: we are confident of continuing to grow strongly in India in the range of higher-teens and also achieving a consolidated sales growth of low-to-medium te ens

items.statement: India Engineering EBITDA margin guided at 20-22% sustainable range for FY27
items.quote: In general, we expect the margin in the range of 20-22%. Yes, as a normal sustainable margin.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at Rs. 50-80 crores; total Rs. 180-200 crores over FY27-FY28 for Bhayla Phase-2 and China Phase-2 expansions
items.quote: we at least expect in the range of Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 80 crores as a year-over-year CapEx

items.statement: China Phase-2 brownfield expansion on track for commissioning by Q3 FY28; full impact from FY29
items.quote: This project should be commissioned by Q uarter 3 of next financial year and we should see a full impact from FY2029 onwards.

items.statement: Bushing sales target ~30% YoY growth to ~Rs. 165 crores in FY27 (vs Rs. 127 crores FY26)
items.quote: fairly confident of achieving targeted sales growth of Bushing around 30% this year against last year's Rs. 127 crores.

items.statement: Stamping sales target ~30% YoY growth to ~Rs. 78 crores in FY27 (vs Rs. 60 crores FY26)
items.quote: we could achieve about 30% growth this year as well in the Stamping against the sales of Rs. 60 crores last year.

items.statement: Large-size Cages targeting 50% YoY growth in FY27 despite weak Q1 (Rs. 10 crores) due to strong order book
items.quote: we should achieve a good 50% growth in spite of 1st Quarter numbers and financial year. Over the last year, we did about Rs. 49 crores.

items.statement: India Engineering Q1 FY27 exports at Rs. 139 crores, up 22% YoY and 11% QoQ; broad-based industrial and auto demand
items.quote: Our export from India in Quarter 1 FY27 stood at Rs. 139 crores. We have reported almost 22% gr owth on a YoY basis and 11% growth on a quarter-over-quarter basis.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 India Engineering margin declined QoQ due to 8% raw material cost increase (lagged pass-through), Rs. 4 crore FX loss, Rs. 3 crore indirect material inflation
items.quote: In Quarter 1 of this year, our average raw material costs have gone up by around 8%. As you are aware, we follow a pass -through mechanism in most of our systems. However, there will be a lag of one or two quarters.

items.statement: Raw material pass-through lag ~4 months; Q1 saw 6-7% RM price increase, 40-50% impact on sales price
items.quote: Usually, as we know, we have a pass -through with around 4 months left. And here I will say, as we discussed in the call, the last year was major pass-through happens in the brass while steel was range bound.

items.statement: Romania subsidiary losses to reduce to low single-digits (Rs. 2-4 crores combined with China) in FY27 vs Rs. 10 crores FY26; new CEO appointed, targeting cage mix increase to 30-35%
items.quote: the combined loss between the two foreign subsidiaries should reduce to much lower single -digit figures if not become fully positive.

items.statement: China Phase-2 expansion debt funding secured at attractive rate; construction commenced
items.quote: We have already commenced the implementation of a Brownfield expansion project in China after securing required debt funding at a very attractive rate.

items.statement: Harsha Advantek targeting Rs. 140+ crores revenue in FY27 (vs Rs. 43 crores FY26) and PAT positive by end FY27
items.quote: Annual sales target in Advantek should be in the region of about Rs. 140 crores plus. This year, Rs. 43 crores achieved last year in FY26. So, as the scale of operations goes up, we expect Advantek to be PAT positive by the end of FY27.

items.statement: China subsidiary guided at ~10% revenue growth in FY27 (vs Rs. 120 crores FY26) with 12-14% EBITDA margin and ~6% PAT margin
items.quote: We believe that Harsha China should report an overall growth of around 10% in current financial as against the sales of about Rs. 120 crores achieved in FY26, with an EBITDA margin in the range of 12 %-14% and a decent PAT range of around 6%.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 standalone EBITDA margin guided at 22-25%
items.quote: But we are still guiding for EBITDA margin of anywhere between 22% and 25% for the full year on our stand-alone financials.

items.statement: CDMO/CMO revenue growth guided at 40-50% YoY in FY27
items.quote: We have guided for a 40% to 50% growth, and we are quite confident that we will achieve that growth in this current financial year.

items.statement: Xanthine revenue guided at INR 900-1,100 crore for FY27
items.quote: But it will be a range between INR900 crores to INR1,100 crores. In that range, I think anywhere it can land INR900 crores to INR1,000 crores, right?

items.statement: CDMO active projects at 57 (37 commercial, 20 developmental) across 22 customers
items.quote: We are presently working with 22 customers and the number of active projects is now 57, of which 37 projects are in the commercial stages, while 20 are under different developmental stages.

items.statement: Company-level gross margin ~50%; CDMO commercial gross margin 60-65%; API gross margin 45-50%
items.quote: Gross margin should be around 50%, plus or minus a few percentage here or there.

items.statement: Xanthine prices elevated vs pre-war; China rebate removal structural, raw material spike temporary; 50-50 split estimated
items.quote: I think the involution duty currently looks like permanent structural change, at least for the near term. For the next few years, I don't see that to change significantly. And in terms of raw material increase - that is temporary and that is basically tied up with the West Asia crisis.

items.statement: Xanthine sales mix shifting to more Cola/beverage customers (74% of volume) with new capacity commitments
items.quote: We are selling more towards the Cola customers than the regular customers because as our new facility is up-ending, we have a higher commitment to give more volumes to these customers.

items.statement: API pricing pressure persists; launching process intensification and cost reduction project for existing molecules
items.quote: While we are working on the development of new molecules with the medium-term patent expiry, the pricing pressures in existing molecules remain. And to mitigate these headwinds, we are starting a special project towards process intensification and cost reduction of existing products.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 3.8% in Q1 FY27 from 1.48% in Q1 FY26 and 1.94% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: As a result of consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 3.8% compared with the 1.48% of Q1 last year, and 1.94% of Q4 of last financial year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 2.67% in Q1 FY27 from 1.65% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The EBITDA margin improves from 1.65-2.67%.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT margin improved to 2.39% in Q1 FY27 from 0.5% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The consolidated margin improved significantly to the 2.39% compared with the 0.5% in Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Pet food market seen as growing opportunity; company in initial stage with separate research team for product development
items.quote: We see a good opportunity in pet food market, and we are working on a separate research team for product development to see the more possibility where we can increase our export.

items.statement: Other income increase driven by foreign exchange gains, duty drawback, and interest on fixed deposits
items.quote: With other income, we have earned basically from the foreign exchange gain. It also from the duty drawback, and also from the interest on the FDs what HMA will have with the certain banks.

items.statement: Focus on sustaining growth momentum, improving operational efficiency, strengthening market presence, optimizing profitability, and maintaining disciplined financial management
items.quote: Going forward, our focus will remain on sustaining this growth and momentum, improving operational efficiency, strengthening our market presence, optimizing profitability, and maintaining disciplined financial management.

items.statement: ISCS EBITDA margin to reach 9% in Q2 and 9.5-10% by Q4 FY27
items.quote: No, we will sequentially improve the margin. And I am fairly confident that in Q2 itself, we will achieve 9%.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 30 bps to 7% in Q1 FY27; ISCS at 8.1%, GFS at 4.1%
items.quote: On the profitability front, our adjusted EBITDA grew by 34% year-on-year with margins expanding by 30 bps to 7%.

items.statement: GFS EBITDA margin target 4.5-5% (currently 4.1%)
items.quote: GFS we saw a 4% EBITDA margin. And ideally, we would expect this to be about 4.5% to 5%.

items.statement: Fuel cost increases passed through to customers in contracts across geographies
items.quote: The way we do the contracting with the customer is that as and when there is a fuel cost increase, it is passed on to the customers.

items.statement: No equity dilution from subsidiary mergers as all are 100% owned
items.quote: At an overall level, there will be no dilution because all these things are 100% subsidiaries of TVS Supply Chain Solutions.

items.statement: FIT 3PL kept separate for GST reasons; not part of merger plan
items.quote: We would like to keep it as a separate legal entity instead of merging it with the parent company.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue of INR121 crore grew 60% YoY, in line with previous quarter guidance
items.quote: For the quarter under review, revenue from operations stood at INR121 crores registering a strong growth of 60% Y-o-Y with a revenue growth in line with the guidance shared in the previous quarter

items.statement: Strong order book for Q2 and Q3; July-August order kitty full after IIJS show with good buyer growth and new family jeweller additions
items.quote: We have seen a good order backing. I think Quarter 2, we think that because of the orders and all, we are hoping that performance will be very much in line with whatever we have projected in earlier commentaries

items.statement: Demand outlook positive for Q2 and Q3; July good, August steady; Q3 led by retail with all stores operational; occasion wear demand resilient
items.quote: The demand side looks to be good and promising for Quarter 2, as we are approaching. And Quarter 3 will be led by retail, and in Quarter 3, we are all our stores are going to be operational

items.statement: Sanctioned debt INR300 crore sufficient for 4 FY27 stores; current debt-equity ~0.8:1; targeting 1.5-2:1 via GML as credit rating improves from BBB+
items.quote: Given that we have a sanctioned debt of around INR300 crores. And we are yet to utilize it, which is sufficient for the four stores that is coming in this financial year. By the end of this financial year, we will be still below 1:1 ratio

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY27 guidance: ~23% consolidated revenue growth (ex-new acquisitions), 5% EBITDA margin, 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion
items.value: 23% revenue growth, 5% EBITDA margin, 50% OCF conversion
items.quote: We remain firmly committed to our stated FY27 guidance of consolidated revenue growth of approximately 23% year-on-year, excluding any contribution from new acquisitions, alongside an EBITDA margin of 5% and EBITDA to operating cash flow conversion of 50%.

items.statement: Achieved full-year FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 5% in Q1 itself; focus on sustaining and building further
items.quote: We are pleased to have delivered our full year FY27 EBITDA margin guidance in the very first quarter of the year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 143 bps YoY to 5%; driven by procurement scale, MedTech mix, and low-margin exits
items.quote: Gross margin expanded 147 basis points year-on-year to 11.4% and EBITDA margin expanded 143 basis points to 5%.

items.statement: MedTech revenue on track to cross INR1,000 cr organically in FY27; carries higher gross and EBITDA margins than pharma distribution
items.quote: Our MedTech segment, will continue to be the most important structural lever in our medium-term margin story. MedTech revenue is on track to cross INR1,000 crores in FY27 on an organic basis.

items.statement: Organic revenue grew 19.6% like-for-like in Q1 FY27, comfortably ahead of IPM growth of 13.8%
items.quote: Organic revenue growth for the quarter was 17.8% on a reported basis and 19.6% on a like-for-like basis, comfortably ahead of the underlying pharmaceutical market growth of 13.8%.

items.statement: Not revising working capital guidance based on Q1; will reassess after H1
items.quote: No, we will stay with our guidance. I'm not revising any guidance numbers based on quarter 1 performance. Maybe let's complete 1 more quarter, then we might speak about what could be the rest of the year guidance for second half.

items.statement: Minority stake buyouts (call options) exercisable over 2-5 years; funding source (parent or sub) to be evaluated per EPS impact
items.quote: We will evaluate what is the best way to acquire minority interest, whether to fund from parent company or to fund from subsidiary. We have all the options available.

items.statement: No major acquisitions planned in FY27; focus on consolidation and organic growth; open to compelling opportunities in Q4
items.quote: We are not looking for any major acquisition in FY27. We have the pipeline, but we don't see doing big acquisitions during this year.

items.statement: IPM growth accelerated to double-digits driven by volume growth across therapy areas; sustainability uncertain
items.quote: We are also very happily seeing that kind of higher growth in IPM for last 2 quarters because it used to be like 7% to 9% earlier now move to double digit and primarily driven by volume growth.

items.statement: Targeting INR 3,000 crore of new project launches in FY27, up from historical ~INR 1,500 crore per year
items.quote: Now, a shift from 1500 crores to 3000 crores which is a 100% growth is definitely qualifying for the word accelerated growth.

items.statement: Expecting INR 1,000 crore of pre-sales in FY27: INR 500 crore from new launches and INR 500 crore from ongoing inventory
items.quote: So, we expect about 500 crores of pre-sales from these projects and from the ongoing projects, we expect about 500 crores of the pre-sales in balanced financial year

items.statement: Targeting EBITDA margin of 25-26% for the full year FY27, up from 18.9% in Q1
items.quote: But we expect to maintain EBITDA margin of about 25-26% over the year.

items.statement: Expecting PAT margin of 18-19% to translate into operating cash flow over the project lifecycle
items.quote: So, we expect to generate, as we have been telling all time, we expect to generate about 18-19% of PAT, you know. So, that will transit into the cash flow.

items.statement: Development pipeline reached estimated GDV of INR 12,800 crore across ~4.2 million sq ft saleable carpet area
items.quote: Our development pipeline has now reached an estimated gross development value of approximately INR 12,800 crores, spread across nearly 4,200,000 square feet of saleable carpet area.

items.statement: INR 3,000 crore of projects planned for launch in FY27 across three projects: Malad redevelopment (INR 750 cr), Thane (INR 2,000 cr), and Santa Cruz (launched Q4 FY26)
items.quote: Third quarter of this financial year, we are launching a redevelopment project in Malad this having a topline of around 750 crore and last quarter of this financial year, we are launching Thane project.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin stable at 29.1%; EBITDA margin 18.9% and PAT margin 13% impacted by lower other income and higher employee costs
items.quote: Gross-profit margins remained resilient at 29.1%, demonstrating the strength of our project economy. Operating EBITDA stood at Rs. 28 crores, resulting in EBITDA margins of 18.9%

items.statement: Construction cost inflation absorbed through incremental residential unit pricing; land cost varies 15-50% of GDV depending on location and ticket size
items.quote: So, normally construction cost inflation is absorbed by the incremental rate in the residential units, you know, and it balances out.

items.statement: Q1 pre-sales grew 9% YoY to INR 155 crore; collections healthy at INR 164 crore; no slowdown in customer enquiries or conversions
items.quote: Our pre-sales for the quarter increased by 9% year-on-year to INR 155 crores, reflecting the strength of our project portfolio and continued customer confidence.

items.statement: Redevelopment to form higher share of pipeline due to land scarcity in MMR; expanding into South Mumbai with larger ticket sizes
items.quote: So, redevelopment will be higher because there is a scarcity of land in MMR and also the availability of older dilapidated buildings is much more in abundance.

items.statement: Anand Nagar project (top-3 GDV) deferred to FY29 launch due to height restrictions from wireless station in Dahisar; station shift expected FY27, approvals FY28
items.quote: There is a wireless station currently in Dahisar because of which there is height restriction in terms, on approval front. This wireless station is to be shifted to Madh Marve.

items.statement: May opt for construction finance at lower rates if needed; currently near zero net debt (INR 5 cr, 0.01x D/E); outright projects fully paid
items.quote: We may look at construction finance like all the projects, the outright projects are already paid for. We are currently at almost net debt and if required, we will opt for construction finances

items.statement: Employee base expanded from 213 to 277 YoY to support growing pipeline; BD and launch teams operate separately for continuous land acquisition
items.quote: Employee costs increased as we continued to strengthen our capabilities, with our employee base expanding from 213 employees as of June 25 to 277 employees as of June 26

items.statement: Targeting 20%+ IRR on new project acquisitions; disciplined approach avoiding fancy deals; Finroot (home loans) open to non-Arkade projects, Assist360 (facility mgmt) currently Arkade-only
items.quote: We are going against an IRR of 20% or around and that is what we are looking forward to as well. 20% plus. That is what our historic growth has been.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY27 is INR2,000 crores; PAT guidance is INR260-270 crores
items.quote: Revenue guidance is INR2,000 crores for this financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 lowered to 21-22% standalone (from 22-24%); blended consolidated EBITDA margin expected at 19-20%
items.quote: Earlier we used to give a margin guidance in the range of 22% to 24%. For the current financial year, we have lowered our guidance a bit in the range of 21% to 22%.

items.statement: Total order book stands at INR6,721 crores: INR3,694 crores water/wastewater (INR2,696 crores execution + INR998 crores O&M) and INR3,027 crores renewable/BESS (INR1,948 crores execution + INR1,079 crores IPP/O&M)
items.quote: Our total order book stands at approximately INR6,721 crores providing strong revenue visibility for the coming periods.

items.statement: Water/wastewater EBITDA margin expected at 21-22%; renewable (solar, wind, BESS) EBITDA margin at 15-18%; blended consolidated EBITDA margin expected at 19-20% for FY27
items.quote: Water and wastewater treatment segment we expect EBITDA margin somewhere in the range of 21% to 22%. And in the renewable segment which spans over solar, wind and BESS, the EBITDA margin shall be in the range of 15% to 18%.

items.statement: Raw material cost increase impact estimated at 1-2% of topline; price variation clauses linked to WPI/CPI cover part but some cost absorption required
items.quote: The raw material price impact is somewhere in the range of 1% to 2% of the overall topline of the company.

items.statement: Water/wastewater bidding pipeline at INR3,000 crores under evaluation plus INR6,000-7,000 crores invited for bidding; renewable wind EPC targeting INR600-800 crores additional orders
items.quote: Presently, the projects for which the bids are already submitted and for which the evaluation is going on, it is somewhere in the range of INR3,000 crores. Apart from this, there is a robust pipeline which is available in form of bidding. So, we are looking for projects somewhere in the range of INR6,000 crores to INR7

items.statement: Suyog Urja second tranche of INR100 crores payable after FY27 (around July) based on KPIs; funded via internal accruals and acquisition debt
items.quote: The second tranche of INR100 crores will be paid after FY27, sometime July. So, it will be based on the KPIs which we have freezed in terms of the revenue, the bottom line and the order book which will be available.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance for FY27 at INR2,500 crores (20% strike rate on INR6,000-7,000 crores pipeline); INR256 crores already secured in Q1
items.quote: The strike rate of company in the last financial year has been in the range of somewhere around 20%. So, we can expect an order inflow of somewhere around INR2500 crores to be there in the current financial year.

items.statement: Suyog Urja revenue target for FY27 at INR400-450 crores; wind EPC order pipeline at INR800 crores with additional INR500-600 crores expected
items.quote: Our expectation is in the range of INR400 crores to INR450 crores what we will do as revenue from Suyog Urja Limited.

items.statement: Long-term growth target of 25-30% CAGR with healthy margin maintenance; not pursuing low-margin projects
items.quote: We look forward to a continuous growth of somewhere around 25% - 30% which should be bare minimum at which the company should keep on growing and with maintaining the healthy margin levels.

items.statement: Overseas and desalination bids submitted; awaiting outcomes; expect these in scope by end of FY27; geographical presence now in 17 Indian states
items.quote: Going forward, we have already submitted bids overseas. We are waiting for the outcomes and we are again looking forward to some desalin projects as well.

items.statement: Expect ~20% quarterly revenue growth for FY27
items.quote: So, we are expected to grow in the same around 20-odd percent quarterly growth for this financial year. It is what we feel will happen.

items.statement: EBITDA margin will not go below 34% for FY27
items.quote: So, we believe that the EBITDA, overall EBITDA will not go below 34%.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin above 34% by FY28-29
items.quote: We expect more by the year '28-'29.

items.statement: Capex guidance of Rs. 70-80 crores for FY27
items.quote: And the Capex will again be something around Rs. 70 crores to Rs. 80 crores this year.

items.statement: Plan to add 3 hubs and 7 spokes in FY27 (in addition to 3 hubs and 6 spokes already opened)
items.quote: Yes. So, the upcoming is 3 hubs and 7 spokes. Sorry. 4 hubs and 7 spokes.

items.statement: Hub capex Rs. 10-10.5 crores; spoke capex Rs. 1.5-2 crores
items.quote: Typically for us, for a hub center, it takes around Rs. 10 crores to Rs. 10.5 crores. And a spoke center takes Rs. 1.5 crores to Rs. 2 crores.

items.statement: On track to reach 100 centres by FY28
items.quote: Yes, we are on track to open 100 centres by FY '28.

items.statement: Mature centres EBITDA margin 40.9% in Q1 FY27; centres under 2 years turned profitable at 6.5% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Our mature centres delivered a 40.9% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY '27. Centres under 2 years old turned profitable for the first time at 6.5% EBITDA margin from negative 5.5% last quarter.

items.statement: Genomics business margin currently 15-20%
items.quote: Genomic margins right now would be somewhere around 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Revenue per test increase driven by mix change, no price hikes
items.quote: No, it is due to the mix change. We have not increased any prices.

items.statement: Switched main biochemistry from Siemens to Roche, negotiated better deal lowering COGS
items.quote: And we have shifted our main track or the main biochemistry business from Siemens to Roche. There also we have negotiated a better deal. And therefore, the margins are also expanding a little where cost of goods sold is concerned.

items.statement: Genomics demand growing due to personalized oncology; Genexus equipment (only one in Eastern India) reduces turnaround from 14-17 days to 48 hours
items.quote: You see, the demand for genomics is going to keep on growing because as we basically accept the fact that oncology treatment is getting personalized, so almost all oncology specimens will need genomic study.

items.statement: Genomics revenue Rs. 13.7M (136% YoY), 80% B2C / 20% B2C split; expect B2B share to grow
items.quote: The vertical recorded a revenue of Rs. 13.7 million, registering a 136% year-on-year growth with five consecutive quarters of sequential growth.

items.statement: Repeat rate appears lower (40%) due to new patient influx from expansion; absolute repeat numbers not declining
items.quote: No. So, basically, as we are expanding our reach, new patients numbers are increasing. And therefore, the repeat patient looks to be smaller, but not if I look at the absolute numbers, they are not degrowing.

items.statement: Order book increased to INR 699 crores primarily on S&P order book providing strong revenue visibility
items.quote: Our order book has increased to INR699 crores primarily on the back of S &P order book, providing strong revenue visibility for the quarters to come.

items.statement: H-Xtreme heat exchanger gaining traction, expected to see significant traction in thermal solutions segment and emerging industries like solar, green hydrogen, semiconductors, carbon capture in coming two quarters
items.quote: So therefore, we believe that this product will start to see a lot of traction in the coming two quarters, especially in our thermal solutions segment and emerging industries such as solar, green hydrogen, semiconductors, and carbon capture applications as well.

items.statement: Strong order inflows across core segments reflecting technology portfolio strength and increasing demand for sustainable water and environmental solutions
items.quote: We are witnessing very healthy order inflows across core segments, reflecting our strength of our technology portfolio and the increasing demand for sustainable water and environmental solutions.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA negative INR 149 million vs negative INR 9 million in Q1 FY26 due to supply chain disruptions and talent investments
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at a negative INR149 million compared to a negative INR9 million in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: European ZLD order of EUR 600,000 to be delivered in Q3 FY27 with better export margins than domestic
items.quote: So, the revenues will come this year, in fact, it's a quick delivery. We should be able to deliver in Q3. It's roughly about a EUR600,000 order that we have got.

items.statement: Supply chain disruptions from Middle East conflict impacted Q1 revenue by INR 50-55 crores (INR 15 crores trading, INR 42-43 crores manufacturing)
items.quote: So, if you look at our trading segment, I would say we lost about INR15 odd crores of revenues. And I think in the manufacturing, we had almost about INR42 crores to INR43 crores of orders that were totally down. So, about INR50 crores, INR55 crores was the overall impact for the quarter.

items.statement: Roserve Water as a Service platform performing well with marquee projects, gaining traction as industries seek asset-light sustainable water management solutions
items.quote: As industries increasingly looking for asset-light and sustainable water management solutions, Roserve is emerging as a compelling offering that supports our broader objective of building recurring and annuity-style revenues.

items.statement: Steel sector seeing major ZLD traction across large players, especially in Odisha, with waste pickle liquor treatment solution demonstrated at largest steel manufacturer
items.quote: So, I think steel is somewhere where we have a very good solution because if you look at the installations that we have done so far as compared to most of our competition, we have really been able to demonstrate how well it works.

items.statement: Supply chain stabilizing from July, expect Q2 to be in growth phase subject to next six weeks stability
items.quote: So, supply chain is getting back to normal. We expect things to be better. So, it should end up in a growth phase, but I would still say that it's subject to some of the things playing out over the next six weeks.

items.statement: FY27 overall revenue growth guided at 20-25%, tractor revenue 25-30%, crane revenue 15-20% from existing plant
items.quote: The company maintains the guidance given earlier and expects to achieve overall revenue growth of around 20–25% for financial year 2026–27.

items.statement: FY27 standalone EBITDA margin guided at 12.5-13%, consolidated similar to last year at 14-15%
items.quote: EBITDA margin is expected in the range of 12.5% to 13% on a standalone basis.

items.statement: Bhud site new plant civil work in full swing, machinery orders placed and ready, commercial production expected by end of November FY27
items.quote: Commercial production is expected to start within this financial year itself, and we are expecting that it can begin by the end of November.

items.statement: Tower crane prototype developed and tested successfully, commercial production in current financial year
items.quote: We have already acquired the technology, as explained in the last call and have now successfully developed and tested our first tower crane prototype.

items.statement: First lot of 10 tower cranes expected to be completed in Q2 FY27 subject to receipt of imported components
items.quote: We expect to complete these 10 machines within this quarter, subject to receipt of the few components we are expecting from outside.

items.statement: Crane margin normalization expected from Q2 FY27 as cost increases from emission norms transition fully passed on to customers
items.quote: From this quarter onwards, because demand has increased, I think everything can be passed on to the customers.

items.statement: Price hikes taken in crane segment, further hikes planned in coming months; tractor price hikes in line with industry
items.quote: Yes, some price hike we have taken in the past also, and a further price hike will be taken in the coming months.

items.statement: Crane demand improving in July-August, emission norms transition phase cleared, expecting 15-20% growth from existing plant
items.quote: Seeing the numbers for July and August, and the kind of response we are getting, growth will start coming.

items.statement: Tractor utilization at 35-40% assembly, 80-85% machine shop; crane capacity 1,200 units currently, new plant adds 3,600 units
items.quote: The new capacity is 3,600 cranes, yes.

items.statement: Dealer network expansion gated by production ramp-up; crane dealers to grow from 25 to 60+ over 1-1.5 years, tractor dealers at 225
items.quote: We have a roadmap to appoint approximately 60-plus dealers to cover the whole country, and once the new plant starts delivering, I think we are on track to reach there.

items.statement: New crane plant 30% utilization in first year (FY27), targeting 70-80% utilization in 3 years
items.quote: In the first year, we will take around 30% capacity utilization of the new plant, and we will increase it from there.

items.statement: Barota Finance penetrates ~20% of new Indo Farm tractor sales, balance is refinancing of old tractors of all brands
items.quote: We are financing around 20% of new Indo Farm tractors. The balance is refinancing of old tractors of all brands.

items.statement: Tractor growth 35%+ YoY for last 3-4 quarters, guided 25-30% for FY27, driven by dealer expansion and NBFC support
items.quote: This year, in tractors, we are expecting growth of around 25% to 30% year on year.

items.statement: Capex spend of ~₹45 crore deposited in banks to be utilized by March FY27, phased machine purchases based on production needs
items.quote: By March, we will consume everything.

items.statement: FY27 operating EBITDA margin guided at 15-17% and PAT margin at 11-13%
items.quote: We expect operating EBITDA margin for FY27 to be in the range of 15% to 17% and PAT margin in the range of 11% to 13%.

items.statement: Medium-term growth target of 30-40% beyond FY27 as execution across multiple fronts gathers pace
items.quote: Looking beyond FY27, we are targeting a sustained growth momentum of 30% to 40% in the medium term as execution across these multiple fronts gathers pace.

items.statement: Pump order book at 22,025 pumps with near-term pipeline of ~12,500 pumps across PM KUSUM, Magel Tyala, and exports; solar EPC order book at ~72 MW with 359 MW pipeline
items.quote: The company's pump order book stands at 22,025 pumps as on date, near a near-term pipeline of approximately 12,500 pumps across direct PM KUSUM, Magel Tyala, indirect PM KUSUM and export orders.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA margin at 15.7% (down 747 bps QoQ) due to 9% realization drop in Magel Tyala, module sales diversification, and elevated input costs
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR74 crores, translating in a margin of 15.7%. The reduction in margins was primarily driven by three factors: Industry-wide competitive bidding under the Magel Tyala scheme, which led to a 9% reduction in realization.

items.statement: PM KUSUM 2.0 expected to launch in current quarter (Q2 FY27) per industry and ministry signals; management confident but cautious on timing
items.quote: Based on the positive and encouraging news coming from the Ministry, we are quite confident and certain that it will be rolled out.

items.statement: FY27 presales growth guidance of upward of 20% year-on-year
items.quote: For the full year FY27, I would like to reiterate that we are committed and very, very confident that we will be delivering a presales growth of upward of 20% year-on-year.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 17% to 19%
items.quote: EBITDA margin, as I mentioned earlier, the guidance for EBITDA margin is between 17% and 19%.

items.statement: FY27 ROCE guidance of 20% or upward
items.quote: And the return on capital employed will be 20% or upward of that.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded to 13% from 11% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The EBITDA margins also, compared to Q1 FY26, expanded from 11% to 13%.

items.statement: Owned land projects margin 25-26%, JDA projects margin 20% at steady state
items.quote: If you look at our own land, it is in the range of about 25%-26%, and as far as the JDAs are concerned, it should be 20%.

items.statement: Total GDV INR52,000 crores; JDA GDV INR27,000 crores (52%); Owned land GDV INR25,000 crores
items.quote: Our total GDV, which is the gross development value, now stands at INR52,000 crores.

items.statement: Demand remains strong across all brands and micro-markets; Q1 presales exceeded internal expectations
items.quote: The demand as of now looks pretty strong in all the projects that we have launched, and we are not seeing any significant change in our projections as far as demand is concerned.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 presales: 64% from JDA projects (MMR), 36% from Thane owned land
items.quote: Out of that 64% contribution came from these JDA models asset-light. So now our presale, if we look at the entire bouquet, clearly the expansion through the asset-light JDA model has proven our point.

items.statement: Internal debt-to-equity cap of 1x; current net debt INR824 crores (0.7x); AIF/SPV funding available as alternative to debt
items.quote: We have maintained an internal discipline of not going beyond 1:1 as far as debt-to-equity is concerned.

items.statement: Parel JDA project GDV INR8,500 crores; launch in ~18 months; ticket sizes INR6-20 crores
items.quote: We also secured a flagship JDA project in Parel during this period with an estimated GDV of INR8,500 crores.

items.statement: Two Mahim JDA launches planned in FY27: Q3 (~INR2,500 crores GDV) and Q4 (~INR2,100-2,200 crores GDV)
items.quote: The first one should get launched towards the latter part of Q3, and then Q4 we will have the second Mahim which will launch.

items.statement: MSME remains core at INR1,395 cr AUM (81% of book); vehicle finance INR131 cr; construction/LAP INR90 cr; wholesale INR58 cr; personal loans INR49 cr
items.quote: On product mix, MSME remains our largest vertical at around INR1,395 crores of AUM followed by vehicle finance at around INR131 crores AUM, followed by construction and loan against property at around INR90 crores

items.statement: Credit cost rose to 0.95% from 0.58% YoY due to vehicle finance portfolio stress in older vintages; gross NPA 2.08%, net NPA 0.93% both improved sequentially
items.quote: Credit cost of the quarter was INR3.69 crores or you can say 0.95% compare with 0.58% in Q1 FY26. The increase was primarily attributed to our vehicle financing portfolio

items.statement: Plan to add 30-35 branches in FY27 across existing states; 10 added in Q1; branches reach breakeven in 7-9 months at INR1.5-2 cr AUM
items.quote: This year we are planning to expand into 30 to 35 branches across the existing states. And in quarter 1 we have already added 10 branches

items.statement: Plan to raise INR300-350 cr equity in FY28 (mid-year) to support leverage expansion to 3.5-4x from current 2.57x net D/E
items.quote: We have a plan to raise capital in next financial year we will start next financial year mid we will start the process and all and we have a plan to raise further capital around INR300 odd crores

items.statement: AUM grew 28% YoY to INR1,721.7 cr; own book up 31.7% to INR1,626.9 cr; customer base 43,946; 194 branches across 6 states
items.quote: Our asset under management stood at INR1721.7 crores as on Q1 '27, representing a growth of 28% year-on-year. Our own book increased by 31.7% to INR1626.9 crores

items.statement: Revenue expected to exceed FY25 levels
items.quote: As far as revenue is concerned, we expect it to exceed FY '25 numbers.

items.statement: Targeting EBITDA margin improvement above current 6.9%
items.quote: Definitely, we are targeting more.

items.statement: Container deployment to start Q3 FY27; CAPEX program substantially complete in FY27
items.quote: Container deployment will start from Q3. We remain on track substantially completing this CAPEX program during FY '27 as guided in our previous call.

items.statement: Added 260 new customers; repeat customer rate 75%; top-5 concentration down to 29%
items.quote: We added 260 new customers and our repeat customers were approximately 75% during the quarter. At the same time, the contribution from the top 5 customers was around 29% of the revenue.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in Middle East causing minor price and supply impact, mitigated by Asia-centric trade lanes
items.quote: There is an impact, but it is not like a major as we see with the other trades in the market. I would say there is a minor impact in terms of price, in terms of supply availability and all those things. But it is mitigated in the right way.

items.statement: Target top-5 customer concentration at 15-20% over next 2-3 years
items.quote: We are expecting it to be 15%-20% because we are diversifying the customer base. We wanted to increase the number of customers and decrease the customer concentration.

items.statement: Air freight to become a major growth driver; no specific revenue target given
items.quote: Going forward, more contribution will come in terms of revenue as well as in terms of final numbers, air will be giving a major boost. I can't comment exactly on which number we will be there in next 2 years but the importance is given into air products to develop.

items.statement: Network expansion planned in Hyderabad, Kolkata, Ahmedabad
items.quote: We are planning to expand in other markets like Hyderabad, which is one of the things we are concentrating into and more importance will be given into the regions like Kolkata. Right now, it has been just an operating office. So Kolkata, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad; these are the regions which will be even more field-focused

items.statement: Trade receivable days improved to 77 from 87 at FY26 end
items.quote: Our trade receivable days stood at 77 days at the quarter end compared to 87 days at the end of FY '26. So this reflects the beginning of the normalization we had flagged in our last call as our newer customer accounts move into the steady billing cycle.

items.statement: Aims to double patented product share in B2C from ~20-22% over 3 years; launching herbicide and potato products to fill gaps
items.quote: Our aim is to almost double it over the period of 3 years.

items.statement: Gross margins improved due to higher share of specialty/differentiated products; expects EBITDA 12-13% for the year
items.quote: Overall, the realization in the business has been better. The gross margins have improved. This improvement is broadly due to the increase in the product mix that is there wherein we have moved more towards our specialty and differentiated products.

items.statement: Backward integration plant at Dahej, Saykha capitalized in Q1 FY27; technical capacity utilization 70-75%, formulation 25-30%
items.quote: the capitalization of the backward integration plant that we have at Dahej, Saykha, which was not capitalized in the last quarter currently correspondingly the depreciation has also increased.

items.statement: Kharif season shaping well with good monsoon in July; acreage up for cotton, soybean, chillies; expects strong Q2 demand
items.quote: But now, by God's grace, in July everywhere it is a raining well and good and up till now, overall, almost a few areas has left, otherwise overall monsoon is good and even acreage of key crop, like cotton has increased, even soybean has increased, even in -- even this year chillies are increasing, so even paddy is almo

items.statement: Raw material cost volatility from geopolitical issues and 10-11% rupee depreciation; B2B able to pass on costs, B2C has time lag but inventory covers it
items.quote: Secondly, due to the depreciating rupee from the last quarter almost the depreciation is 10% -- 11%. So, because of which also there is some impact that we are seeing on our raw material prices.

items.statement: Cautious on Brazil due to liquidity/credit challenges; some orders lost to China on logistics speed; South India monsoon still wait-and-watch
items.quote: Brazil, we are seeing we are a bit cautious also because we have seen liquidity issues in Brazil where is the credit is also a challenge.

items.statement: Domestic revenue split: 80% domestic (45% B2C, 45% B2B), 20% exports; expects branded to reach 45-50%, B2B 30-35%, exports ~20% in 3 years
items.quote: We see that going forward 3 years, this kind of a mix would broadly continue. We expect the branded business to go to 45%-50% whereas remaining say 30%-35% will be then the B2B business. Export broadly for the upcoming 3 years will be somewhere around 20% only.

items.statement: Other income INR8.3 cr in Q1 includes INR5.7 cr one-off land sale; no further land sales planned; normal run rate lower
items.quote: Out of these INR8 crores, almost INR5.7 crores is this other income for the land sale that is under consideration which you specifically mentioned. There is no other income that we plan that will be there in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: ICRA upgraded rating from A to A+ stable / A1 due to IPO loan repayment and continued performance
items.quote: ICRA has upgraded our rating from A to A+ stable for our long-term as well as short-term facilities for A1. This upgrade is majorly due to the repayment of borrowing from our IPO and the continued good performance of the company.

items.statement: Management expects to double revenues in FY27 driven by full Netcom consolidation and AI ramp-up
items.quote: We should be able to try and double our revenues this year, and that's what we are currently embarked on.

items.statement: AI revenue contribution expected to become sizable within 12-18 months as ResolX deployments scale
items.quote: We should be able to see a good amount of revenue showing up in a horizon for about 12-18 months or probably even slightly more.

items.statement: Plans to acquire two more companies over next three years targeting Fortune 500 clients in North America
items.quote: In the next three years, we intend to try and acquire another two companies that are on our radar. But this time, we're looking at companies which have Fortune 500 brands, and that can really bring us to the largest spectrum of North America.

items.statement: 12 live ResolX deployments across 7 enterprise clients in insurance, aviation, banking, automotive, digital assets
items.quote: We're seeing encouraging early traction, 12 live deployments across seven enterprise clients spanning across insurance, aviation, banking, automotive, and digital assets.

items.statement: Strong pipeline with 10-12% conversion rate across LATAM, North America, India; banking, insurance, healthcare, travel showing traction
items.quote: Currently, we are hovering around a good 10-12% of our conversion. We have an active pipeline across all cohorts.

items.statement: Resolution-as-a-Service model prices based on cost per resolution vs traditional headcount/hour model; 30-40% deflection/absorption to human achieved in deployments
items.quote: The overall deflection or absorption to human is close to about 30-40% depending upon the use case where we've deployed this.

items.statement: Debt of INR 220 crore at ~9% cost from Netcom acquisition; strong cash flows expected to service and repay debt
items.quote: We have only taken exposure of debt in acquisition of Netcom, and their effective cost of around 9%. As Akash sir explained earlier, our company has a strong cash flow position, and we have planned out our debt repayment schedule.

items.statement: AI deployed in airline case reduced employee needs by ~30% while adding value-added services
items.quote: We've been successfully being able to deploy AI to seek benefit about 30% of the employee size, and thereby bringing far more value-added services to them.

items.statement: Volume growth target of 25% for FY27 based on new plant ramp-ups and auto sector growth
items.quote: The 25% is our definitely our internal targets. We have invested in two plants at Tirupati and Odisha which are ramping up and also some brownfield expansions and also the growth of our existing customers. So everything put together we definitely believe that yes we should be able to achieve the 25% growth

items.statement: EBITDA per kg guidance maintained at INR12/kg on sustainable basis despite Q1 achieving INR12.40/kg
items.quote: While internally we do target increase in this EBITDA margin but for the guidance to the street we are maintaining INR12 as the EBITDA margin on a sustainable basis.

items.statement: Invested INR53 crores in Q1 FY27 on greenfield projects at Shoolagiri and Bawal; capacity to exceed 7 lakh tons by end FY27
items.quote: During the quarter we invested Rs. 53 crores in greenfield projects at Shoolagiri and Bawal, while also advancing brownfield projects and technology led initiatives at Tirupati and other locations. These projects are progressing as planned and are expected to take our installed recycling capacity beyond 7 lakh tons per

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA per kg improved to INR12.40/kg from INR12/kg guidance; GP margin improved to INR27,450/ton from INR26,000/ton in FY26
items.quote: And the EBITDA with all this improved slightly to INR12.40 per kg or INR12,400 per ton.

items.statement: Aluminium prices rose ~40% QoQ (INR226-230/kg to INR350/kg) causing negative operating cash flow due to higher working capital needs
items.quote: Average sale price was nearly around INR226/kg to INR230/kg in last quarter and in this quarter INR 350/kg. So around 40% prices has been increased. Therefore, the working capital requirement also increased. So overall my cash from operation is negative.

items.statement: Auto sector remains key driver with PV and 2W sales up 26% and 20% YoY in Q1 FY27; EV penetration at 8.26% in FY26; Ather Energy added as new EV customer
items.quote: The automotive sector continues to be a key growth driver for CMR with passenger vehicles and two-wheeler sales growing nearly 26% and 20% year-on-year respectively in Q1 FY27, while India's EV penetration reached 8.26% of total vehicle registrations in FY26. We are well positioned to participate in this transition wit

items.statement: Targeting volume mix rebalance from 66-10-24 (auto/non-auto/other metals) to 60-20-20 over coming year for more diversified earnings
items.quote: In FY26 our volume mix stood at 66% automotive alloys, 10% non-automotive, and 24% other metals. And we actually aim to rebalance it to 60-20-20 over the coming year creating a more diversified and resilient earnings profile.

items.statement: Scrap sourcing becoming challenging due to export restrictions by some countries; mitigating by expanding domestic and import sourcing base
items.quote: Look, sourcing of scrap is getting challenging. There are countries which are putting restrictions on export of scrap from those countries. So it is becoming more challenging. How we are doing is that we have expanded our sourcing base and frankly while on the growth projections that you have we trust that we will not

items.statement: Inventory days reduced from 45 to 40 QoQ; cash conversion cycle improved from 69 to 65 days; AI-enabled import tracking system implemented
items.quote: We have gone to about 40 days of inventory from 45 days that we recorded in the previous quarter. And we have actually reduced our cash conversion cycle to 65 days in this quarter from about 69 days in the last quarter.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio currently 0.86 vs historical 0.5 target; expected to normalize as prices stabilize and working capital cycle improves
items.quote: Working capital cycle and another is a debt equity ratio. So historically we maintain the 0.5 debt equity ratio and we also in future will maintain the same ratio. But currently it is around 0.86. So definitely it will come down when the prices have got stabilized.

items.statement: India's aluminium extrusion industry expected to grow 12% CAGR through FY29; EPR framework to increase min recycled content from 5% in FY28 to 10% over time
items.quote: India's aluminum extrusion industry is expected to grow at 12% CAGR through FY29, driving demand for recycled billets, while the UBC ecosystem continues to expand with improving collection infrastructure and rising circular packaging commitments.

items.statement: Hindustan Zinc JV still at MOU stage; no construction started; will take time to finalize
items.quote: As far as Hindustan Zinc is concerned, we have signed an MOU with them but there is nothing definitive which has still been finalized. So, no activity for construction of a plant has yet started. We are still in discussion with them. So, it will take a while before things move there.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY27 maintained at INR 1,200-1,250 crores, implying ~25% growth over FY26's INR 1,007 crores
items.quote: We had given a revenue guidance of 1,200 to 1,250. We'll still hold to that as of today because the pipeline looks good.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 expected to remain muted; growth recovery hoped for in second half of FY27
items.quote: Next quarter is also looking, you know, muted, I think second half of the year, we are hopeful of seeing some growth.

items.statement: Sales pipeline increased to USD 28 million from USD 25 million last quarter, with shift toward higher-quality outcome-based deals
items.quote: Vikas, the number is 28 million.

items.statement: Employee and resource costs (currently ~77% of total costs) expected to decline as percentage of revenue over time due to outcome-based contracts and AI-driven engineering efficiency
items.quote: Percentage of overall employee and resource costs vis-a-vis revenue, we do expect it to decline in terms of percentage to revenue over a period of time.

items.statement: Top clients not normalizing spending; significant disruption from AI and industry headwinds continues
items.quote: Nothing is normalizing. Okay, there is tremendous disruption because of AI, there's tremendous disruption in the industry because of headwinds, competition.

items.statement: Voluntarily letting go of tail accounts with no scaling potential; top-10 client concentration reduced from 58% to 56%
items.quote: No, we are letting them go, Vikas, because accounts that we don't feel have any potential to scale or we are in a situation where we are marginalized, we are just letting go.

items.statement: Larger IT competitors moving downmarket for smaller deals, but AI enables Saksoft to access larger RFPs previously out of reach
items.quote: Competition, has gone up for sure, because larger companies are also competing for smaller deals. But vice versa is more relevant for us, deals where we were not present, we are now present because of AI.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin stable at 18.26% with EBITDA of INR 45 crores (down 1% YoY) on revenue of INR 249 crores
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR45 crores, reflecting a marginal decline of 1% year on year, while the EBITDA margins remained stable at 18.26%.

items.statement: Employee strength at 2,434 (2,223 technical); utilization at 83%; 16 clients with $1M+ annual revenue
items.quote: Our total employee strength stood at 2,434, out of which 2,223 were technical professionals. The employee utilization, excluding trainees, remained healthy at 83% during the quarter.

items.statement: PLA plant commissioning expected: lactic acid in October, PLA in December; targeting ~40% average capacity utilization in Q4 FY27 (Jan-Mar)
items.quote: So, Sanjay, as far as commissioning goes, it looks, you know, lactic we should be able to commission in October and PLA in December.

items.statement: Sugar inventory of 45.67 lakh quintals at avg carrying cost INR 37.19/kg as of June 30 provides favourable base for upcoming quarters
items.quote: As of June 30, the Company was carrying sugar inventory of 45.67 lakh quintals at an average carrying cost of INR 37.19 per kg.

items.statement: PLA project capex spend of INR 2,180 crore by end of July; construction in full flow with civil, equipment arrivals, erections ongoing
items.quote: We have spent about INR 2,180 crore by the end of July. Alongside project execution, we have made encouraging progress on product development, customer trials, and market engagement.

items.statement: Season 2025-26 tighter than anticipated with lower production, healthy domestic consumption and ethanol diversion drawing down inventory
items.quote: The season 2025-26 has turned out to be tighter than anticipated, with lower than expected production, healthy domestic consumption and diversion towards ethanol resulting in a drawdown to inventory.

items.statement: Domestic sugar prices firming up due to tight demand-supply, providing relief and offsetting higher sugarcane and distillery margin pressures
items.quote: This tighter demand-supply balance has led to firming up of domestic sugar prices, providing relief to millers and helping offset higher sugarcane costs and other costs & margin pressures in terms of distillery, especially.

items.statement: Assume no B-heavy/juice diversion allowed next season; only C-heavy permitted. Cane price hike likely given state elections. Net impact expected positive
items.quote: Hence, going into next year, though nothing has been done, it is reasonable to assume that there will be no diversion allowed towards B and juice. So that is a reasonable assumption today.

items.statement: Q1 distillery margins resilient due to B-heavy and maize feedstock mix; juice-based ethanol sales minimal. Transfer pricing impact affected by seasonal cost allocation
items.quote: In the quarter gone by, it was largely B-heavy and the maize-based ethanol. There was hardly any sale on account of juice-based ethanol. That is the reason margins are at a good level.

items.statement: Monsoon progress and crop yields across key states will clarify 2026-27 production outlook by end of September; El Niño impact on East UP cane crop considered overblown
items.quote: The progress of monsoon, crop development and yields across key producing states, we will get clarity over the next few months. The first meaningful clarity is expected around the end of September.

items.statement: Cane sowing area flat but yields look much better for 2027 season; rainfall in command area ideal for cane so far
items.quote: Yes, but the area may be kind of flat, but the yield looks much better.

items.statement: Sugar price base has moved up firmly and sustainably; higher realizations expected to offset cane price hike and distillery diversion ban net-net positive
items.quote: So we know the sugar price base has moved up. All our assumptions, as I said, when we know. We know cane price might go up. We know distillery may be banned from making B-heavy or juice. Keeping all these variables together on a single page and trying to work out numbers, I am not thinking that we will end up very nega

items.statement: Closing stock normalization to ~45-50 lakh tonnes by Oct 2027 if no diversion allowed next year and production ~31 MT, consumption ~29 MT; sugar prices expected north of INR 43/kg
items.quote: Probably in one year, because if they do not allow diversion next year, and assume the gross production is 31 million tonnes, consumption is 29 million tonnes and 3-odd million tonnes is the closing stock. Give or take 5 lakhs tonnes here and there, 5 lakhs tonnes on the upward side. Even if consumption is to move a li

items.statement: Overall capex for FY27 remains approximately INR 300 crores as stated in May call
items.quote: Overall capex for the year will still be what I mentioned in the May call, approximately INR 300 crores for the year.

items.statement: Draw tower expansion accelerated from phased 4-6-8 million km to direct 4 to 8 million km in one go due to global fiber shortage
items.quote: But in the meanwhile we have decided to go ahead with the complete expansion right from four to eight in one go, seeing that there is a shortage of fiber across the globe and that shortage is likely to continue for some time more.

items.statement: Preform production commenced, targeting stability in next couple of months; 100 metric ton facility for captive use
items.quote: On the expansion side, I had mentioned in the last call that the preform production has commenced. We are on the way to stability. Hopefully in the next couple of months that should happen.

items.statement: Communication cable revenue INR 176 crores in Q1 FY27 (62% YoY), exports INR 35-40 crores to US and Europe
items.quote: Communication Cables delivered a particularly strong performance during the quarter with a revenue increase from INR 109 crores to INR 176 crores, which is a growth of approximately 62% with margins close to 30%.

items.statement: Communication cable margins near 30% in Q1 due to low-cost opening inventory; will normalize to low-double digits as inventory depletes
items.quote: But as that stock gets depleted, you will see a correction in the margins. I still believe that at the end of the year provided the demand situation remains similar to what it is today, I still believe that you should have a double-digit margin number, it'll probably be in the low-double digit numbers.

items.statement: Electrical cable margins sustainable at ~10.5%
items.quote: On the domestic front, the margins at electrical cable side should be sustainable. We are at about 10.5% I think, and those should be sustainable.

items.statement: Fiber prices (G.652.D) peaked at USD 17-18/km, now settling at USD 11-13/km; premium fibers up to USD 50/km
items.quote: The standard fiber, which is the technical term there is G.652.D, was somewhere around USD 5 to 6 back in December last year, had climbed up to USD 17 - 18 over the last six, seven months. I think currently is settling at about between USD 12 and USD 13 per kilometer that's where it is today.

items.statement: Copper rod plant shut in Q1 due to LPG availability restrictions; price hike of ~3% taken in May
items.quote: During the quarter, we changed prices once. We revised it upwards once, that was I think in May, we took it up by about 3% or so.

items.statement: JV revenue INR 87 crores, profit INR 7 crores in Q1 FY27, continuing profitable trend
items.quote: The additional information that I would like to share with you is that I had mentioned that the JV was doing well and had posted a profit of INR 24 crores last year that trend continues in the current quarter. They generated a revenue of about INR 87 crores with a profit of about INR 7 crores.

items.statement: FMEG target of INR 5 billion revenue by FY28 maintained despite Q1 supply constraints (LPG, PVC) impacting fans and conduit pipes
items.quote: But the target of INR 5 billion by 2028 still remains and we are sure that we can get over there.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of INR 9,400-9,500 crore and EBITDA of INR 670-680 crore
items.quote: And company as a whole, for the year, the numbers we told you earlier, we are holding ourselves on that same number, around INR9,400 crore to INR9,500 crore total revenue, and INR670 crore to INR680 crore EBITDA company as a whole, Surya Roshni, will do.

items.statement: Steel segment FY27 EBITDA per ton guidance of INR 4,600-4,700 for full year
items.quote: And we are fully committed that full year of FY27 guidance of INR4,600 to INR4,700 per ton EBITDA will be achieved.

items.statement: Steel segment Q2 FY27 EBITDA per ton expected at INR 4,400-4,500; H2 combined at INR 4,600-4,700
items.quote: We will do around INR4,400, INR4,500 in the second quarter and combining third and fourth quarters, we will achieve an EBITDA per ton of INR4,600 to INR4,700 for the full year.

items.statement: Steel volume target 11 lakh tons for FY27 with quarterly ramp: Q2 2.6-2.65 lakh, Q3 2.8-2.9 lakh, Q4 ~3.2 lakh tons
items.quote: In the full year, our volume target is of 11 lakh tons. Currently it is at 2.3 lakh tons, In Q2 we will do around 2.6 lakh tons, in Q3 2.8 lakhs to 2.9 lakh tons, and in Q4 around 3.2 lakh tons.

items.statement: Steel order book at INR 800 crore including 78,000 tons export API orders for US; combined with lighting order book totals INR 1,000 crore
items.quote: Our order book across trade, export, API, and spiral pipe stood at INR800 crore, including 78,000 tons of export API orders for the US market.

items.statement: Steel EBITDA per ton Q1 FY27 at INR 4,006 vs INR 2,922 YoY; impacted by INR 800/ton ocean freight and INR 200/ton input cost increase
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at about INR84 crore, up 63% year-on-year, with EBITDA per ton to INR4,006 against INR2,922 in Q1 of FY26.

items.statement: Ocean freight impact INR 3,800/ton on exports in Q1; new orders booked at higher freight rates, expecting INR 600-1,000/ton EBITDA improvement in coming quarters
items.quote: First, because of ocean freight, there was an impact of nearly INR3,800 per ton in this quarter. And our total exports have been over 20% in this quarter. If I divide that by total volume, there is an impact of nearly INR800 per ton on EBITDA purely because of ocean freight.

items.statement: Buyback under consideration post double taxation correction; decision expected within 2-3 quarters; demerger also under board evaluation
items.quote: No, work is going on regarding that. Hopefully, very soon, we will make some decision on that. But as such, I don't have any material today to disclose but our team is working on it. Because now, the double taxation angle that was there earlier has also been corrected by the government.

items.statement: Monsoon revival in July improved agri input demand outlook ahead of rabi season; fertilizer demand strong but constrained by availability as many companies not operating at 100%
items.quote: The demand is definitely going to be strong in the current quarter. And we are also coming new season -- the rabi season is really strong in the Northern states.

items.statement: Switching production away from negative-margin NPK/APS to economically viable products; importing ammonium sulphate; caprolactam-benzene spread >$800 supports caprolactam production
items.quote: Whatever product we can produce, which are economically viable, that we have switched over from the basket where there is negative contribution or negative margin.

items.statement: Melamine production nil in Q1 due to high NG cost and cheap Chinese imports; approached GOI for anti-dumping duty/minimum support price
items.quote: As far as melamine is concerned, due to the higher NG rate, 38% increase in the NG rate also. So that molten urea is used in the melamine production and that melamine production cost is not met.

items.statement: Cash position tight in Q1: INR500 crore borrowings at June-end; INR500 crore subsidy outstanding; funds deployed in raw material/finished goods inventory for rabi season
items.quote: So yes, you can say there is no cash surplus in the June. So there was a INR500 crores borrowings at the end of the 30 June.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 13-15% for the year given crude prices and reinvestment in growth
items.quote: given the crude prices, I have said that the EBITDA margin would be in the range of 13% to 15%.

items.statement: Underlying gross margin estimated at 39.5-40% after adjusting for inventory impact and promotional spend reclassification
items.quote: the underlying gross margin and maybe Krishna will also walk through it. It was closer to about 39.5% to 40%.

items.statement: Premium decorative segment (45% of business) drove 25% volume growth; adjacencies grew faster but mass market lagged
items.quote: our largest contributor, 45%, comes from premium. So, if premium doesn't grow in the 20%, we cannot do a 25% volume growth. So, very clearly driven by decorative premium.

items.statement: Project Akshaya integration with JSW Paints targeting cost synergies; ERP migration by year-end; cross-manufacturing and supply chain redesign underway
items.quote: savings of around 2.4 crores was realized, which was part of the first initiatives, part of the P&L which was presented to you.

items.statement: Price hikes taken in line with industry; benchmark pricing vs market leader not new entrants; distributor commissions 4.5-4.7% included in rebates
items.quote: We benchmark ourselves on pricing versus the market leader, because we believe that the industry is fairly pretty disciplined.

items.statement: Expect to catch up on delayed export dispatches over next 3 quarters; domestic volume growth of 20% seen achievable, export depends on freight normalization
items.quote: assuming that we - not assuming actually that we haven't dispatched enough in the first quarter for our exports, we should be able to catch up with optimism over the next 3 quarters, the dispatches of the order.

items.statement: Domestic market volume growth of 20% expected; export volume recovery contingent on freight situation
items.quote: As of today, on the domestic market, yes. But export market, it depends on how the situation moves in international market on the freight. Otherwise, domestic market, as of today, yes, we see that type of volume growth.

items.statement: Export order book encouraging but dispatch slowed by vessel non-availability and high ocean freight; no order cancellations, only delayed call-offs

items.quote: The first is raw material inflation, primarily aluminium and related alloys. These costs are contractually pass-through in nature and are fully recoverable from customers, albeit with the timing lag.

items.statement: Indian auto industry strong: PV +11.3%, 2W +21%, CV +19.5% in Q1 FY27; Alicon grew 37.7% consolidated, 17.5% volume-adjusted
items.quote: If we adjust the impact of material inflation, our underlying volume or growth is approximately 17.5% on a consolidated basis, and 22% on a stand-alone basis.

items.statement: Hybrid segment seen growing 25-30% CAGR, EV 20-22% CAGR over 4-5 years; Alicon single-source supplier to largest Indian hybrid OEM
items.quote: Our current assessment is that the hybrid segment could grow an approximate 25% to 30% CAGR over the next several years, while EVs could grow at approximately 20% to 22% CAGR over four to five years of time.

items.statement: Non-auto order book 2% (Rs 126 crore) of Rs 8,450 crore; new vertical created, early wins in data center HVAC housings and tractor aluminium cylinder heads
items.quote: Out of this order book of Rs. 8,450 crore, we see at this moment, the non-auto visibility is 2%. So, this is roughly around Rs. 126 crore.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated tonnage 9,124 tons (Europe ~150-200 tons); FY26 full-year tonnage 34,000 tons
items.quote: So, if I say we have done 9,124 tons, only 150 tons to 200 tons is what we do in Europe. So, it is very miniscule at this point of time.

items.statement: Expects 1% margin improvement in FY27 over FY26 adjusted margin of 11.4%
items.quote: I explained to you, in this year, we are expecting to improve by 1%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 reported margin 9.5% vs 11.4% last year; adjusted margin 11.4% after removing aluminum impact
items.quote: This quarter, we have the margin of 9.5% against 11.4% for the last year. But I have also explained that the adjusted margin is 11.4% for this quarter when we remove the impact of the aluminum.

items.statement: Aluminum price increases are passed through immediately with back-to-back pricing from 1 April; no future lag impact
items.quote: Just for aluminum. That is right.

items.statement: Freight cost increases partially passed through; some confirmed, some under discussion to conclude this quarter
items.quote: Some increases are already accounted for, which we have already got a confirmation, but some are in discussion, which we should be able to conclude in this quarter.

items.statement: JLR EV dispatches started; currently supplying 600 sets/week, expected to increase from Jan 2027; peak by Q3 CY2026
items.quote: Currently, we are expected to supply them at a rate of 600 sets per week. And we already have an indication from JLR that this number would further increase from Jan 2027.

items.statement: Order book split: EV 16%, hybrid 12%, structural (common to ICE/EV/hybrid) 10%, remainder ICE and 2-wheeler
items.quote: In this pie, the electric vehicle is around 16% and hybrid is around 12%.

items.statement: Intentionally reducing 2-wheeler market share by 1-2% to allocate capacity to higher-value PV, industrial, defence products
items.quote: We have intentionally reduced our market share in 2-wheeler segment by 1% to 2%. And this is basically because we want to allocate the capacities now for higher-value products.

items.statement: New Pune plant (135,000 sq ft) possession 1 Sep 2026; SOP by Mar 2027; Rs 125 cr capex to generate Rs 500 cr revenue in 4-5 years; tonnage 3,000-7,000 tons
items.quote: We are looking for going in SOP into this factory by March 2027 or just towards the end of the financial year. And in terms of capacity, as I have said, we are looking for generating a revenue of around Rs. 500 crore in this factory.

items.statement: Capex payback typically 3-4 years; ROCE was 10.7% in FY26, targeting 15% with minor tweaks; JLR investments currently loss-making but turning around this year
items.quote: Generally, in our kind of setup, the paybacks are generally typically 3 years to 4 years, which is quite impressive.

items.statement: New order book more concrete vs past; focused on traditional ICE/hybrid parts with shorter validation vs complex EV parts; Rs 8,450 cr revenue target by 2030 includes last 3-4 years additions
items.quote: This is around Rs. 8,450 crore. This is already included in that. What I only mentioned is these are the very recent developments which are either in the last quarter or slightly before that.

items.statement: Data center opportunity: starting with one customer in India, expanding to Europe and Mexico in next 2 quarters; 7-8 aluminum parts identified; multiple customers targeted
items.quote: They have already confirmed in the next 2 quarters, they are going to open up the Europe market and thereafter Mexico.

items.statement: Aspiration to reach 14-15% margins long-term; team working aggressively but no specific timeline given
items.quote: Yes, there is a possibility. And I can only tell you that these are some of the aspiration numbers the team is working hard towards.

items.statement: Machining share currently 65-70% of PV tonnage; will increase with in-house machining investments
items.quote: At this moment, this is in tune to 65% to 70%.
