items.quote: We are also getting positive signals from the field, and we believe that this development would accelerate procurement activities in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Q1 revenue mix 60% defense / 40% civil vs typical 70/30; defense has higher margin due to EW resilience requirement
items.quote: Today, because EW resilience is a necessity on the defence side, that business has more margin contribution than the civil business, which is not delivering an EW resilient product.

items.statement: Supply chain pressure on thermal cameras and electronic components causing timeline delays; not currently impacting customer delivery commitments
items.quote: Due to the current ongoing geopolitical conflicts, there is a pressure on the supply chain of thermal cameras and the electronic supply chain also is seeing a certain pressure where the timeline delays are happening.

items.statement: YETI middle-mile logistics UAV completed tethered hover test; designed for 6,500m takeoff altitude, 200kg payload; only platform with this capability
items.quote: YETI, in my opinion, is the only platform in the world from whatever we have searched that is designed to take off at 6,500 meters takeoff altitude.

items.statement: Q6 V2 GEO received DGCA Type Certification; 6 platforms now type certified; enables GIS, mapping, urban planning, digital twin use cases
items.quote: Our Q6 V2 GEO received DGCA Type Certification, opening up advanced GIS use cases across large-scale mapping, urban planning and digital twin applications. Six of our UAV platforms are now type certified by DGCA.

items.statement: Advancing combat capabilities: air-launched effects, fuel-hybrid ZOLT, loitering munitions, long-range strike platforms with partners; targeting upcoming large defense opportunities
items.quote: In Q1, we made significant progress in the development of combat drone capabilities like air-launched effects and fuel-hybrid long-endurance capability for ZOLT. We are also in advanced stages of developing combat capabilities like long-range strike platforms and loitering munitions along with our partners.

items.statement: Deployed fleet crossed 1 million customer missions; drone takes off every 2 minutes globally; operates in extreme altitudes, temperatures, EW environments
items.quote: I'm elated to share that during the quarter; our deployed fleet crossed the milestone of 1 million customer missions. Across our fleet today an ideaForge drone takes off somewhere in the world every 2 minutes.

items.statement: US operations: focusing on JV operationalization and Blue sUAS certification; exploring USD30M+ defense programs; international NFR orders from partners in Europe, Middle East, South America, Africa
items.quote: In fact, I feel that at least one of the programs that is live right now is about a USD30 million program, where they have many players who will be participating.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance retained at 20%+ (implying >INR10,000 cr vs FY26 INR8,430 cr); will revisit after Q3
items.quote: We remain focused on achieving 20%+ value growth for the financial year, building the Senco brand across the country, reaching more customers and expanding through both owned and franchise stores, with a geographical focus on East and North India.

items.statement: Added 3 COCO, 4 franchise, 1 Sennes store in Q1; 12-15 more stores planned for rest of FY27, majority franchise, focused on East and North India
items.quote: In terms of new stores added during the quarter, we added 3 company-owned, company-operated stores, 4 franchise stores and 1 Sennes showroom focused on lab-grown diamonds. The company remains on track to open another 12 to 15 stores during the remainder of the financial year, and these are very much in the pipeline.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 7% (INR213 cr) vs guided sustainable 7.5%-7.8%; impacted by gold price fall, discounting, old gold exchange; customs duty gain ~INR12-15 cr
items.quote: As noted in our comments, this quarter's margins were affected by the fall in gold prices, competitive intensity and discounting, partly offset by the customs-duty impact. That is the broader context in which the 7% EBITDA margin should be viewed.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 reported 10.1% EBITDA included 1.5-2% inventory gains; adjusted PAT ~INR70-75 cr vs Q1 FY27 PAT INR101 cr
items.quote: Q1 last year benefited from a price rise, and we clarified at the time that although the reported EBITDA margin was 10.1%, our sustainable EBITDA margin was between 7.5% and 7.8%.

items.statement: Customs duty increase benefit estimated at INR12-15 cr in Q1 (45 days impact); further benefit expected over next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: We estimate that the customs-duty gain in Q1 was around INR12-15 crores. This benefit will be partly offset by customer schemes, discounts and other promotional measures, but INR12-15 crores is the estimated gross range for the quarter.

items.statement: July-August tracking ~25% YoY growth, 8-10% above May-June run rate; Q2 seasonally softer, focus on inventory build for festive season
items.quote: As we move through July and August, we are seeing a substantial improvement in consumer sentiment and in customers' inclination to buy jewellery and prepare for their festive and wedding requirements.

items.statement: Hedging maintained at ~50% under Board policy due to volatility; intend to move toward 75-80% as conditions stabilise; GML availability constrained in Mar-Apr, now normalised
items.quote: Our hedging strategy is guided by the Board-approved policy. At present, we are maintaining hedging at approximately 50% because the last financial year saw extreme volatility. We need to balance liquidity risk with the risk of gold-price movements.

items.statement: Other expenses rose to INR195 cr (from ~INR80 cr) on store renovations, customer schemes, brand building; management says this run rate will not continue and will subside in upcoming quarters
items.quote: Exactly. This run rate will not continue, and we expect it to subside in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Inventory days at ~152; improved stock turnover by end of Q1; will build inventory again from September for festive season
items.quote: Inventory days are currently around 152, as stated in the presentation. We will continue to work on improving this further.

items.statement: Sennes (lab-grown diamond, perfume, leather) and Dubai subsidiary in start-up phase, weighed on consolidated PAT (3.3% margin)
items.quote: However, the Sennes brand is still in its start-up phase and is developing its lab-grown diamond, perfume and leather-bag businesses. Any new brand takes time. Sennes Fashion Limited and the Dubai entity therefore partly affected consolidated PAT, which was nevertheless at a margin of 3.3%.

items.statement: Launched Aham men's jewellery collection combining titanium with gold/diamonds, priced INR20,000-1 lakh; among first in industry with titanium jewellery
items.quote: I can proudly say that, consistent with Senco's focus on innovation, we are among the first in the industry to launch titanium jewellery. While gold and diamonds are incorporated in the jewellery and contribute to margins, the addition of titanium keeps the overall price range affordable. The range starts at about INR2

name: Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth to exceed FY26's 37% YoY; EBITDA margin target upwards of 24%; ARPOB growth 9-10% YoY
items.quote: I think we have said that last year, we grew 37% Y-o-Y. As you can clearly see this year, we will easily surpass that growth even the EBITDA is concerned. I think the company is on track close to upwards of 24% EBITDA margin for the full FY27 is concerned. And I think similar is the ARPOB growth and the PAT parameters.

items.statement: ARPOB growth guided at 9-10% YoY for FY27
items.quote: I think 9% to 10% is the right estimation to be taken.

items.statement: Capex per bed for next 1,800 beds estimated at INR 75-80 lakhs; Gurugram at ~INR 1 crore per bed
items.quote: I think the capex per bed should be around INR75 lakhs to INR80 lakhs capex per bed, which includes the greenfield, the brownfield, the acquisitions.

items.statement: Bed capacity target of 5,000 beds to be achieved in ~2.5 years (earlier than 3-year target); 3,200 beds already announced/under construction
items.quote: I think it should be even less than three years. So, we did mention last time around three years, so as we also mentioned that we will be surpassing that target much earlier as 3200-bed capacity is already visible and it's already announced.

items.statement: New hospitals (Faridabad Sec 20, Model Town) to reach 15-20% EBITDA within 15-18 months post-breakeven; mature units at 25-27%
items.quote: Both these 2 hospitals, from here, we are targeting, let's say, around 15 months, once they get breakeven, the EBITDA there could be somewhere around 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Room rent capping recommendation viewed as non-material risk; government historically supports private sector; past price caps (stents, implants) absorbed
items.quote: So far, we have always seen that government, in fact, has always supported the growth of private hospitals. In fact, for the first time after a lot of years, CGHS's rates were also revised. So, we feel in the past, government has always backed the private sector as well.

items.statement: Occupancy at mature Noida/Jhansi hospitals at 90%+; Greater Noida 74%, Noida Extension 56% with improvement expected; new hospitals ramping volumes
items.quote: Our existing hospital occupancy reached approximately 75% as inpatient volume improved 15% year-over-year. As far as hospital-wise occupancy is concerned, Noida and Jhansi-Orchha Hospital achieved 90% plus occupancy.

items.statement: Oncology contributing ~10% of group revenue; adding LINAC at Faridabad Sec 20 and New Delhi to strengthen oncology; surgical mix improving in new hospitals
items.quote: Oncology has already started contributing close to 10% to the group's revenue with only one LINAC machine currently at Noida Extension Hospital. We are in the process of adding another LINAC at our Faridabad Sector 20 hospital soon, followed by the New Delhi facility.

items.statement: PAT margin pressure from higher depreciation and interest cost due to recent capex (Gurugram, oncology machines); pressure to ease as capex slows
items.quote: I think it's because we have done certain high capex over last few months as far as the acquisition of Gurgaon and the construction is going on. Also, we have recently ordered for oncology machines for both Faridabad and Model Town. So, a lot of capex has been done in this quarter and a bit of bank debt increasing sinc

items.statement: Debt increased from INR 210 Cr to ~INR 300 Cr (INR 80 Cr for acquisition); future capex funded via internal accruals and debt; comfortable with 2x TTM EBITDA leverage
items.quote: If you see that we have a debt in our books in March of nearly around INR210 crores which is now being increased to around INR300 crores. Basically, it has increased because we have partly taken the acquisition fund from the debts around INR80 crores.

items.statement: Model Town Hospital EBITDA breakeven expected between Q3-Q4 FY27; Faridabad Sec 20 achieved breakeven in Q1 FY27 (9 months)
items.quote: Model town, we are expecting it to break even, somewhere around, between Q3, Q4 this year, so that will also reduce the drag on EBITDA.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion at Greater Noida and Noida Extension (450 beds) to start coming live in 15-18 months; Gurugram (250 beds) live by Q1 FY28
items.quote: We feel, as mentioned earlier in the fall, somewhere around 15 to 18 months in the capacity will start coming live for the Brownfield capacity expansion.

items.statement: EBITDA per TEU expected to remain around INR 2,400 level going forward
items.quote: Going forward, we expect EBITDA per TEU to remain around INR2,400 level.

items.statement: Target EBITDA per TEU of INR 2,750 in 3-year plan including Farukhnagar ICD
items.quote: In our 3 years plan, we have targeted EBITDA per TEU of INR2,750. That's including Farukhnagar project.

items.statement: Endeavor to maintain EBITDA per TEU in range of INR 2,400 to INR 2,500
items.quote: We will endeavor to maintain profitability, EBITDA per TEU numbers in the range of INR2,400 to INR2,500 per TEU.

items.statement: Total capex plan of INR 400 crores over 3 years (Plan 2030), with INR 100 crores in FY27
items.quote: Close to INR100 crores of that capex we should incur in the current financial year, '26-27.

items.quote: by end of this financial year, we will be the cash positive. If we commission 650 megawatt of this solar NOPL

items.statement: Total identified portfolio of 3.63 million sq ft across 40 centers with 52,000+ seats, including 1.13M sq ft operational, 0.19M under fit-out, and 2.31M signed for future
items.quote: This takes our total identified portfolio to approximately 3.63 million square feet across 40 centers and operational seats being more than 52,000.

items.statement: Ahmedabad development management project requires ~INR 100 crores fit-out investment for 8.6 lakh sq ft yielding 8,500 seats and ~INR 120 crores revenue potential
items.quote: Once the building is ready and handed over to us, we will do investments into the capital towards fit-outs, which would be roughly around INR 100 odd crores, following which our property operations would commence with approximately 8,500 seats and it has a potential to generate revenue of roughly INR 120 odd crores.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 56.3% (Ind AS) and 23.2% (IGAAP); standalone EBITDA margin 66% (Ind AS)
items.quote: Our consolidated EBITDA under Ind AS increased by 14.7% on a year-on-year basis to INR 30.3 crores, with EBITDA margin improving to 56.3% from 47.4% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Raised INR 100 crores via 11.75% secured NCDs (36-month tenure); 1.85 crore shares (19.65%) encumbered but promoter holding unchanged at 36.81%, expected to rise to 37.29% on warrant conversion
items.quote: Subsequent to Q1, DevX raised INR 100 crores through senior, listed, secured, redeemable, and non-convertible debt, carrying a coupon of 11.75% per annum with a tenure of 36 months.

items.statement: FY27 guidance: 3.5-4 GW sales, INR 6,000 cr revenue, ~12% EBITDA margin, 6-7% PAT margin
items.quote: So our guidance remains as was given earlier, between 3.5 to 4 gigawatt sales, revenue around INR6,000 crores, with a EBITDA of about 12% and a PAT margin of about 6% to 7%.

items.statement: Phase 1 capex ~INR 1,850 cr (2.4 GW cell + 4 GW module); Phase 2 capex ~INR 1,600-1,700 cr (3.6 GW cell); total ~INR 3,500 cr
items.quote: So the right now the Phase 1 that we have of about 2.4 gigawatt of cell that is approximately and 4 gigawatt of module that is approximately INR 1,850 crores. And the Phase 2 of 3.6 gigawatt of cell would be approximately around INR1,600 to INR1,700 crores.

items.statement: Confirmed order book 6.35 GW (~INR 8,200 cr), 132% of current 4.8 GW module capacity; 70% utility, 30% C&I/open access; 30% DCR orders
items.quote: Our confirmed order book currently stands at approximately 6.35 gigawatts, representing around 132% of our current operational module capacity of 4.8 gigawatt, and providing strong forward revenue visibility.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 8.33% vs 7.25% Q4 FY26; expect significant improvement in H2 FY27 as cell manufacturing ramps up, targeting high-double-digit EBITDA
items.quote: We feel it will be a significant increase in our EBITDA and the bottom-line. Difficult to give a number, but it's going to be in the high-double digits that is what we can say right now.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation (Iran war) driving commodity, logistics, forex volatility; ALMM-2 delay to Jan 2027; policy uncertainty causing customer deferrals; US policy changes raising polysilicon/cell prices
items.quote: The ongoing geopolitical situation and associated supply chain uncertainties continued to influence global markets. Commodity prices remained volatile, logistics costs remained elevated, and foreign currency fluctuations added further variability to the cost environment.

items.statement: Current debt ~INR 1,250 cr; net debt expected to peak at INR 2,200-2,400 cr; debt-to-equity 0.99; capex funded via balanced capital structure
items.quote: So net debt wait what we are looking at would be at around INR 2,200 crores, approximately INR2,200 crores to INR2,400 crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 expected to deliver healthy double-digit YoY growth; full-year H2 outlook uncertain due to high base from September 2025 GST rate correction
items.quote: I think it will be very interesting to see how the market pans out from September onwards, especially when we do a YoY comparison. Because last year, as you recollect, post the GST rate correction, the market really picked up from the month of September. But I think the kind of growth that we have seen in July, it will

items.statement: Indonesia order of 70,000 Yodha and Ultra T.7 units to be supplied over FY27 and FY28; deliveries initiated in Q1 with ~2,000 units shipped
items.quote: I can only say that the 70,000 orders will certainly be supplied over a period of two years, FY27 and FY28.

items.statement: Government bus orders of ~4,500 units on hand for delivery in Q2 FY27; 850+ electric bus orders from private customers and state tenders
items.quote: CV passenger, we still have around 4,500 government orders on hand, which we will continue to deliver during this quarter. As I spoke, there are 850 e-buses orders also on hand.

items.statement: Net price increase of 2.5% taken on July 1, 2026; confident it will pass through in Q2; further commodity cost pressure expected in steel, rubber; first line of attack is internal cost management
items.quote: The net price hike in July, we have taken 2.5% increase and very confident that it should pass through as we progress during the quarter.

items.statement: Underlying demand fundamentals strong per e-way bills (+12.4% YoY), diesel consumption, FASTag collections; correlated with robust GDP growth; July demand robust despite monsoon
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier, Pramod, I think the underlying demand fundamentals are pretty strong, right? We saw e-way bills, diesel consumption, FASTag collection. I think all the indicators indicate very high movement of goods, which means the underlying freight available is pretty robust.

items.statement: EV volumes grew ~3x YoY; SCV EV penetration reached double-digits in May and June; >3,200 SCV EV retails in Q1 (4x YoY); strong customer interest in EV trucks and 850+ e-bus orders
items.quote: EV volumes grew almost three times on a YoY basis. In fact, in SCV pickup, the EV penetration reached double-digit in the months of both May and June, and that continues to improve further as we get into Q2.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 investment spending ₹515 crore (~2.7% of revenue), within guided 2-4% range; capex ₹554 crore vs ₹639 crore in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Total investment spending in Q1 was ₹515 crore at approximately 2.7% of revenue. This sits comfortably within our guided range of 2% to 4%.

items.statement: Supply chain constraints in sheet metal, casting, forgings due to broad-based auto demand surge; debottlenecking actions underway, throughput improved end of Q1 and into Q2; cell supply from China bottleneck for Intra EV, higher orders plac
items.quote: As a result of which, some of the part categories like sheet metal, casting, forgings have become a constraint. To address this, a lot of debottlenecking actions have been taken place, few more in the pipeline, but this has already enabled us to improve the throughput towards the end of Q1 and of course in Q2.

items.statement: Freight Tiger now subsidiary after additional 18.1% stake acquired for ₹96 crore in May 2026 (total 63.6%); integrating with FleetEdge for end-to-end digital logistics ecosystem
items.quote: On Freight Tiger - we acquired an additional 18.1% equity stake in May 2026 for around ₹96 crore, taking our total holding to approximately 63.6%. Freight Tiger is now a subsidiary. The intent here is straightforward, bringing FleetEdge and Freight Tiger together so that it gives us an end-to-end digital ecosystem acro

items.statement: Standalone net cash ₹7,100 crore at June 30 vs ₹7,500 crore at March end after ₹1,473 crore dividend payout; Auto ROCE 68% TTM vs 72% FY26
items.quote: Net cash stood at ₹7,100 crore as of June 30th, against ₹7,500 crore at March-end and this is after the ₹1,473 crore dividend payout during the quarter. Auto ROCE continued to be strong at 68% on a trailing twelve-month basis, against 72% for FY26.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY27 revenue target of Rs 750 crore and EBITDA margin around 17%
items.quote: Let me close my remarks by recreating our guidance of Rs. 750 crores in revenue for FY '27 at an EBITDA margin of around 17%.

items.statement: Q1 revenue of Rs 182 crore represents ~24% of FY27 target, ahead of 45:55 H1:H2 split
items.quote: The 1st Quarter therefore represents approximately 24% of our full-year revenue target of Rs. 750 crores. That is ahead of where the 1st Quarter needs to be, given our guidance that the year splits 45:55 between the two halves.

items.statement: Saicriti facility at Gummadidala on track for April 2027 completion, adds 154.66M units injectable capacity (47% more than original plan)
items.quote: This proposed route delivers approximately 154.66 million units of injectable capacity against approximately 105 million units under the original upgradation plan. That is roughly 47% more capacity on a larger and long-lived asset, at an unchanged CAPEX outlet from the company and with the completion extended only abou

items.statement: Australian facility physical completion targeted January 2027, TGA inspection by March 2027, Phase 1 manufacturing from April 2027
items.quote: Construction is on schedule with physical completion targeted for January 2027. The TGA licensing inspection anticipated by 31st March 2027 and Phase 1 manufacturing expected from April 2027.

items.statement: Contracts have 90-120 day lag for price revisions; recovery of raw material cost increases partial, full benefit expected in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our contracts carry a window of 90-120 days between a price revision being notified and being realized. That lag is now beginning to unwind in our favor. The recovery of raw material cost increases remain partial at this stage, and we expect full further benefit to flow across the contract book through the 2nd Quarter.

items.statement: Noumed holds 5 exclusive long-term contracts and 10 exclusive supply molecule contracts covering 526 SKUs with 5+ year terms
items.quote: Today, we hold 5 exclusive long-term contracts and we hold 10 exclusive supply molecule contracts, covering 526 SKUs. The typical terms are 5 years and more.

items.statement: Peak debt expected in FY27 with de-leveraging from FY28; gross debt/equity comfortable at 0.6x; Saicriti project debt at subsidiary level
items.quote: FY '27 is expected to be a peak year of debt growth for the existing business as we complete the ongoing CAPEX and Acquisition Program with de-leveraging from FY '28 as these assets begin to contribute to earnings and cash flows. Even at peak debt, the gross debt to equity ratio is comfortably placed at 0.6 times.

items.statement: Prathyak Labs acquisition brings 65-person R&D team (28 scientists), 150 SKUs across 86 molecules in complex injectables (lyophilised, liposomal, nano, oncology)
items.quote: Prathyak operates an established research and development center at the Genome Valley in Hyderabad with 3 years of operating history, 65 personnel including 28 research scientists and a pipeline of 150 SKUs across 86 molecules with proven capability in lyophilised, liposomal and nano-based complex injectables and in on

items.statement: US subsidiary incorporation approved for preliminary market entry evaluation; no timeline or strategy finalized
items.quote: The Board also has approved the incorporation of the subsidiary in the United States to be held as a step-down subsidiary through Sai Parenterals PTE Singapore. The entity is being created to support the company's evaluation of an entry into the United States market. This evaluation is at a preliminary stage.

items.statement: Guided FY27 revenue growth of 20-25%, similar to FY26 trajectory
items.quote: So this year we will be keeping a same growth trajectory what we have posted last year, around 20% to 25% growth range we will be trying to keep.

items.statement: Current order book of INR100 crores executable in Q2 and partly Q3 FY27
items.quote: Yeah, so like I said, the current order book stands at INR100 crores.

items.statement: Planned capex of INR25-30 crores over 1-1.5 years for Nashik premix facility redevelopment, 70% debt-funded
items.quote: So overall capex -- so as you are aware that one strategic, there is a demolition happening at our Nashik factory for our premix facility, and it is redeveloping with the new infrastructure, for that we will be incurring a capex roughly around INR25 crores to INR30 crores in the coming one year or maybe one and a half

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined to 11.3% in Q1 FY27 from 13.8% in Q1 FY26 due to raw material cost increases from West Asia crisis
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin stood at 11.3% during the quarter compared with 13.8% in Q1 FY '26. The movement in EBITDA margin needs to be viewed in the context of the business and the product mix during the quarter, along with the investments being made to support our next phase of the growth.

items.statement: MRP increased 10-15% on select branded products to pass through raw material cost increases, impact visible from Q2
items.quote: Approx 10 % to 15% we have increased our MRP. So that will see a impact in the Q2 onwards.

items.statement: Strong order book of INR100 crores supports Q2 FY27; historically Q3-Q4 are stronger quarters due to seasonality
items.quote: No, in fact our Q2 is very strongly supported by a strong order book of around INR100 crores. Okay. So there is definitely no sign of a slowdown in the quarter two.

items.statement: Branded segment grew 28% YoY, now ~30% of revenue; target 35% in next couple of years
items.quote: So in the next couple of years we expect that to go to that 35% mark.

items.statement: Capacity utilization improved to 47% blended in Q1 FY27 from ~30% last year; Nashik at 55-60%, Chennai 25-30%, Tuticorin 35-40%
items.quote: So overall, capacity-wise we have seen a volume growth this quarter, which representing around 47% of total capacity utilization at this stage.

items.statement: West Asia crisis increased freight costs and critical raw material prices (whey proteins), impacting gross margin by >3%
items.quote: The major reason is the West Asia crisis where we have seen few of our critical raw materials in our segments in premix as well as branded has seen a rise in the cost.

items.statement: ESG order pipeline of INR75-100 crores for FY27 from national governments and UN agencies
items.quote: Right. So we will be looking at around INR75 crores to INR100 crores. For the year. Yeah.

items.statement: Volume growth of 25-40% YoY in Q1 FY27 across premix and branded segments; price hikes not main driver
items.quote: So overall, if you see the volume mix, the volume has grown roughly around 25% to 40% for this quarter.

items.statement: Field force increased >50% YoY to expand into Tier 2/3 cities; operating leverage expected by Q3 FY27
items.quote: More than 50% of our field force have increased compared to last year Q1. And we see this as an investment which has impacted the bottom line at this moment, but definitely it will add value in the next coming quarters.

items.statement: International growth driven by Central Asia and Africa; targeting Europe and North America expansion
items.quote: Yeah, so we are looking at a good growth in areas like Central Asia and also Africa. And going forward we are also looking for newer geographies which include Europe and North America.

items.statement: Management will not provide formal forward-looking revenue or profitability guidance due to structural uncertainties in approvals, government tenders, and global volatility.
items.quote: We intend to stick to a policy of not providing formal, forward-looking guidance.

items.statement: EBITDA margin for FY27 expected to be similar to FY25-FY26 blended levels (~27%), with less dramatic quarterly volatility than seen in FY26.
items.quote: If you look at '25 and '26, I think there would be reasonable guides for, I mean, we should expect very similar numbers in '27 for EBITDA as a percentage.

items.statement: No significant capex planned for core business in FY27-FY28; only maintenance capex of 5-10% of gross block annually, plus potential debottlenecking if large orders materialize.
items.quote: For maintenance capex, I mean, you can look at, I think at any point in time, it will be a few percentage points, that is required. So, one can say that between 5% to 10% of your gross block at any point in time you can assume is a maintenance capex that you have to keep doing.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue of INR247.2 cr driven significantly by ready parachute contract execution; Q4 FY26 was anomaly due to pulled-forward US exports and parachute shipments.
items.quote: This growth was primarily driven by execution of our ready parachute contracts which scaled meaningfully during the quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 31% (up 900bps YoY) due to richer product mix including parachute contracts; sequential decline from 41% in Q4 FY26 due to lower operating leverage off elevated base.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR75.9 crores at a margin of approximately 31%. Year on year basis, this represents a margin expansion of roughly 900 basis points from the 22% in Q1 FY26, driven by a richer higher margin product mix including the ready parachute contracts.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization 55-60%; large capex came fully online last year, management hopes for full utilization but business growth depends on approvals.
items.quote: However, on utilization, I would be I would say we are currently between I would say 55% to 60% utilization. We did a very large capex, that sort of came fully online last year.

items.statement: Management does not disclose executable order book; orders exist in stages (POs, LOIs, projections) making parsing difficult. FY27 expected to be steady growth year with moderate volatility.
items.quote: At any point in time, sir, we have orders that are in various stages. One is where we have received formal POs, then the second is where we have LOIs, and then the third is where we have projections. It becomes difficult for us to sort of parse these numbers and be able to sir, exactly tell you which of these will get

items.statement: Operating cash flow expected to turn positive in FY27; receivables normalized after Q4 FY26 anomaly.
items.quote: I think it will be positive sir. It is positive only, sir. Yes, sir.

items.statement: Parachute systems executed under licensing agreement with technology partner, not own IP.
items.quote: Yes, they are, so it's under a licensing agreement. That's right. With one of our technology partners, sir.

items.statement: Outdoor & Lifestyle segment capacity not a constraint; growth driven by progressive brand approvals and seasonal volume ramps; brand projections strong but subject to material changes.
items.quote: The outdoor and lifestyle business, I mean, capacity at this point of time is not really a constraint for us. It's progressive product approvals, that brand by brand, customer by customer, we continue to get approvals.

items.statement: Company operates 7 manufacturing facilities (6 Gujarat, 1 UP) with full vertical integration; 1000+ fabric SKUs; 2000+ employees; exports growing.
items.quote: We operate seven manufacturing facilities, six in Gujarat and one in UP, spanning the full value chain from preparatory and weaving through dyeing, printing, finishing, coating, lamination, and fabrication of certain specialized products.

items.statement: Aim to reach 2 million tons LPG distribution volume in coming years, targeting 50% growth rate
items.quote: We have always had aim to reach 2 million tons in distribution in coming times ahead.

items.statement: JNPA Port: executing ~318,100 cbm liquid, 77,236 MT LPG, bottling plant 35k MT/yr at ~INR1,675 crore; Phase 1 (100k cbm) Q3 FY27
items.quote: executing a major expansion of approximately 318,100 cubic meters of additional liquid storage, 77,236 metric tons of LPG capacity and an LPG bottling plant with 35,000 metric tons of annual capacity with a total capital outlay of roughly INR1,675 crores

items.statement: JNPA Board approved 52,000 MT refrigerated double-walled steel LPG tank
items.quote: the Board of Directors in its recent meeting has approved the development of a 52,000 metric ton refrigerated double-walled steel LPG tank at JNPA

items.statement: Targeting gearing ratio ~0.6; funding $5B capex via balanced mix of equity, internal accruals, debt; Aegis Vopak self-funded via equity dilution
items.quote: We'll pursue this growth with disciplined funding through balanced mix of equity, internal accruals and debt, targeting a gearing ratio of approximately 0.6

items.statement: CPG division targets quarterly breakeven in 4-5 quarters via margin-accretive model
items.quote: In terms of a quarterly breakeven for this business, we are working towards another 4 or 5 quarters. We should have a quarterly breakeven on this business.

items.statement: Nutra EBITDA margin steady state expected at 12-15% once scale normalizes
items.quote: From an EBITDA margin perspective, steady state is likely between 12% and 15%.

items.statement: Jaggery plant in Karnataka to commission in 6 months, will more than double capacity
items.quote: The plant will be commissioned in 6 months' time. It is coming up in Karnataka. It will more than double our current jaggery capacity.

items.statement: Jaggery turnover from both plants expected near Rs 100 crore once fully running
items.quote: Once we have both plants running, we should be able to do closer to Rs. 100 crores in terms of turnover, just from both of these plants.

items.statement: Sugar prices moved above Rs 45-46/kg; may correct once crushing starts
items.quote: In the current month, sugar prices have moved well north of Rs. 45-Rs.46 per kg. We will need to wait and see if these hold. Perhaps once crushing starts, it is very likely that there may be some correction.

items.statement: TN/AP cane availability declining; expect flat to 5% drop in crush this season
items.quote: In the current year, yes, probably there is going to be a flat or about a 5% drop in these geographies.

items.statement: Employee cost rose due to VSS at legacy plants; more VSS planned to reduce fixed costs
items.quote: They have gone up because of VSS which we have done. A lot of our legacy plants we are offering VSS. You will see more of that. This is being done with a longer term interest in mind. And overall bringing the fixed cost position down.

items.statement: Ethanol-sugar mix optimized dynamically; 582 KLPD ethanol capacity (120 KLPD grain); OMC commitments limit switching
items.quote: 582 KLPD is our capacity, which is roughly about Rs. 18 crore liters, out of which about 120 KLPD is our grain capacity. In terms of switching between ethanol and sugar that is an evaluated call we have to take depending on the margin profit.

items.statement: CPG shift to value-added products (jaggery, brown sugar) and distribution expansion driving margin pool growth despite revenue decline
items.quote: Yes, value mix shifting more towards value-added. I think you have seen that shift play out in Quarter 1. We will see more of that play out. I think adding new products, jaggery, brown sugar, etc., is a big area of focus.

items.statement: JLR targets 10% revenue growth per annum with significant focus on US market
items.quote: So we are setting a goal of 10% revenue growth per annum and focusing on the US market for a significant part of that.

items.statement: JLR aims to save $1.7 billion on ex-works cost, warranty, and fixed cost base
items.quote: On costs, our focus is the ex-works cost of our cars, warranty, and our fixed cost base. And our intent is to save $1.7 billion in this space.

items.statement: TMPV targets higher double-digit volume growth in FY27, maintaining ~2x industry growth pace
items.quote: We would like to keep that kind of momentum going forward. So, I would definitely be targeting higher double-digit growths in FY 27.

items.statement: TMPV capex at Rs 1,300 Cr in Q1; will step up for next growth phase per Investor Day guidance
items.quote: Our Capex at Rs. 1,300 Cr for the quarter, this is still tracking last year's trends, but we will see it step-up as we execute our next phase of growth in line with our Investor Day guidance.

items.statement: JLR Q1 EBIT margin 2.8%; VME rose to 7.1% driven by China luxury taxes and US market normalization
items.quote: VME in the second big column is significantly higher. It's now at 7.1%. China is the most difficult market year-over-year for us given economic and retailer stress and also the effect of the new luxury taxes that came into force after Q1 last year.

items.statement: TMPV took cumulative 1% price increase (0.5% each in April and July); will take further calibrated increases through year
items.quote: We have already taken a 1% cumulative price increase across April and July and while we will be taking calibrated increases through the rest of the year...

items.statement: TMPV accelerating cost reduction initiatives; achieved 1.5% benefit in Q1, expecting incremental gains in Q2
items.quote: We are also having strong cost reduction programs that we are accelerating. We had a 2% benefit YoY. In Q1 itself, we had 1.5%. We'll get incrementally more this quarter.

items.statement: Revenue growth momentum expected to continue for 3-4 quarters; freight rates rising is positive for freight forwarding
items.quote: I would not put any number, but this growth momentum would continue for coming quarters, three to four quarters, which we have seen in first quarter also.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 275 bps YoY to 9.34% in Q1 FY27; further improvement expected from technology and cost rationalization
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin also improved to 9.34% from 6.59%, effective increase of 275 basis points.

items.statement: Warehousing gross margin is 15-20%; contribution expected to grow from 15% to 17-18% by year-end and ~20% eventually
items.quote: But on absolute margin if you talk about it is 15 % to 16% gross margin at which we operate in the warehousing business, 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Volume growth 6-7% YoY in Q1; rest of 18.4% revenue growth from freight rate increases due to geopolitical volatility
items.quote: If you see the number of shipment, the shipment growth is around 6% to 7% as compared to last year. And rest of the growth has been happen from the freight rates.

items.statement: Asset-light model to continue; investments primarily in technology (AI-based application launched July 1) and selective leased warehousing
items.quote: Whatever the investment will happen will happen primarily means as of now it's primarily focusing on asset-light model only.

items.statement: Ocean export freight rates rising; air freight benefiting from cargo shifting from ocean; this incremental profitability expected to continue 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Incremental profitability in our industry is in ocean exports, if the ocean exports right now going up because the freight rates are going up.

items.statement: Freight rate growth sustainability may not be long-term; volume growth essential for India's export economy
items.quote: The freight growth sustainability may not be very long term. So our growth has been a mix of 6 %, 7% growth in the volume growth and another growth is the freight rate growth.

items.statement: DSO improved from 72 days to 56-57 days; working capital discipline supporting operating profitability
items.quote: At one point of time our DSO or collection cycle increased to almost 72 days, which has come down now to 57 day, 56 days.

items.statement: AI-based application launched July 1 automating 42,000 annual shipments; reducing paperwork, TAT, and manpower costs
items.quote: We have almost we have done 40,000 shipments last year, 42,000 shipments. So we created 42,000 files manually. Now we are basically automating this entire process.

items.statement: Targeting 20% revenue growth for FY27; Q1 achieved 18% growth
items.quote: So the 20%, as I said, that is definitely what we are working towards. And Q1 has been at 18% growth, as far as revenue is concerned.

items.statement: Engineering capex ~INR400 crores for stamping capacity in Gujarat, Gurgaon, Bangalore; land acquired in Gujarat
items.quote: We are investing in Stamping capacity enhancement in Gujarat, in Gurgaon and in Bangalore. So in these 3 places, we -- as you might be knowing, we have acquired land in Gujarat for EV project and Stamping project.

items.statement: Full-year capex for Engineering division guided at INR110 crores
items.quote: The capex is about INR110 crores.

items.statement: Engineering division has LOI from Tata for ~INR150 crores battery project; project on hold pending Tata Group decision
items.quote: We had bagged LOI from Tata, which is about INR150-odd crores. But you might have seen that yesterday, in the newspaper, news related to Tata, Agratas and others, there are issues.

items.statement: Home Appliances PBDIT margin target: early double digits (10%+); Q1 FY27 PBDIT margin 5.79% vs 5.34% YoY
items.quote: So PBDIT should be early double digit in my opinion.

items.statement: Gross margin down ~160 bps YoY due to commodity/forex; cost initiatives offsetting at PBDIT level
items.quote: Our gross margin is down by about 160 basis points because of the material cost increase.

items.statement: AC volume growth 6-8% YoY in Q1 (industry ~20%+); disadvantaged by new energy ratings making products 10-15% costlier; focusing on higher-capacity models
items.quote: The new rating, as you might realize, is about 10% to 15% more expensive than the market. And therefore, we did not have the advantage of the older-rated products with a price advantage in the market.

items.statement: Targeting 50-60% AUM growth for FY27
items.quote: We have committed, that 50 % to 60% of AUM growth at the start of this financial year, we'll continue to, we are continuing to pursue that.

items.statement: Targeting debt-to-equity of 4-4.5x for FY27 with 15-20% co-lending share
items.quote: Our targeted range is about where the industry is right now, which is at 4x and beyond that, we will also have participation in terms of co -lending. Our idea of having a co -lending proportion of at least 15% to 20% by end of this financial year.

items.statement: Investing in compliance software and team for middle-layer NBFC and RBI regulations
items.quote: We got head of compliance as well as a whole team under the compliance set, as well as we are investing in software to ensure that we are fully compliant for both, middle layer regulation as well as new RBI compliance regulations.

items.statement: Yields stable at 20%, targeting 20-20.5%; cost of funds to decline with rating upgrade and co-lending; opex/AUM to fall with scale
items.quote: The yields have been stable at 20%. These yields will not go down, they trying to increase these yields. You can assume that it will it will stabilize somewhere around 20% or 20.5%.

items.statement: Targeting steady-state ROA of 3-3.5% and ROE of 18% over medium term
items.quote: If you ask us ROA, ROE guidance for the next five years, we ideally would want to be at a 3 %, 3.5% ROA and a 18% ROE kind of a number. That's what we are targeting.

items.statement: Gold price correction reduces ticket sizes and industry growth; new branch expansion offsets impact for small NBFC
items.quote: If you look at historically, whenever the gold prices are corrected or subdued, the gold loan industry did not grow to that extent. It has an industry-wide direct correlation.

items.statement: Implemented RBI-mandated segregation of consumption loans (tiered LTV 75-85%) and income-generating loans (board-approved policy)
items.quote: In terms of LTV, that is where the major changes have happened, wherein RBI wanted to segregate clearly between consumption loan and income generating loan. That we have implemented.

items.statement: Gross NPA 0.54%, Net NPA 0.48%; conservative LTV and collateral management protect portfolio despite gold price volatility

items.statement: Care Health Insurance aims to beat market growth; no full-year guidance given

items.quote: So we are still -- in spite of just doing INR150 crores this quarter -- see, our real estate revenue will come only in Q4, all of a sudden. Till then, we will not see it. So we are still confident that we can achieve INR1,200 crores.

items.quote: Looking ahead, we are targeting approximately INR1,500 crores to INR2,000 crores of new EPC order intake during FY27.

items.quote: But this year, Q1, Q2 comprise 30% and Q3, Q4 will comprise 70% of the top line because whatever the slow progress is going on, that is now picking up nicely.

items.quote: Looking ahead, we see a healthy opportunity pipeline across our target markets, growing water security needs driven by urbanization, climate change, industrialization and tightening environmental standards continue to support demand for desalination and reuse, particularly in water stressed regions.

items.quote: With a strong order backlog, diversified execution portfolio, healthy pipeline and robust balance sheet, we remain confident of delivering a sustained and profitable growth for quarters and years to come.

items.quote: See we have already guided for a 15% to 20% growth, Shubham, and we are confident of meeting that. And I'm sure you know that our endeavor will always remain to be better than what we promised.

items.statement: Asset-light model requires no capex for order execution; modular business scales with order size

items.quote: Yeah, see we normally we have order of around 2 months in hand. So, we can see this year target is roughly Rs200 crore Rs180 to Rs 200 crore.

items.quote: we have given guidance that during this fiscal year, we intend to spend about INR 400-odd crore in capex across various businesses. We have not allocated, money specifically towards EV or ICE, but it is fairly, spread across our business verticals as well as divisions.

items.quote: We believe that by Q3 or Q4 things will get normalized because Q2 we are seeing the impact of this situation again.

items.quote: So by quarter three this year, we are expecting to get good in in textile business also. As of now, we don't have any plan for demerger or that kind of thing.

items.quote: Growth was led by direct advertiser demand in structurally expanding sectors like Quick Commerce, BFSI, FinTech, and Retail and by premium omnichannel formats such as connected TV and video streaming.

items.quote: we do expect our occupancy level to touch 30% or up from Quarter 3 or Quarter 4 onwards and we are also likely very confident that on to the Quarter 4 or near Quarter 3 end, we would be able to see a PBT positive number also

items.quote: The pressure on the EBITDA margin is temporary because we have deployed new doctors and new specialties which had come in so it takes some time about a quarter or so that the doctor reflects of its complete profitability into the subsequent quarter we see the EBITDA margin to improve

items.quote: We were earlier expecting 50 to 100 bps. But now we think that these margins are normalized at where we are in case there is no further disruption in the currency and commodity.

items.statement: Fluoropolymers expected to grow 17-20% annually going forward, driven by volume and high-value products
items.quote: Fluoropolymers has done well and expected to grow, as we had said earlier, 17% to 20% annually going forward as well, again, primarily on volume as well as the high- value products.

items.statement: Battery materials revenue to reach 3-digit crores by Q4 FY27 with significant ramp-up in FY28
items.quote: We are on track and meeting our targets, what you said, 3 digit in quarter 4 and significant ramp-up in the following financial year.

items.quote: The Oman project right now, we have put on hold, okay? items.quote: We are already -- our fundraise process is on, and we are raising as we are going along in terms of our fund requirement. items.statement: AHF capacity expansion in phases: first phase by end of FY27/Q3, subsequent phases matched to refrigerant capacity additions
items.quote: It will be in different phases. The first set of capacities will be there probably by the end of this year or the third quarter. And then subsequently, every quarter, some capacity will be added because it will be matched with our refrigerant capacity being added.

items.statement: R32 expansion expected to reach full utilization of 20,000 tons during calendar year 2027
items.quote: Yes, we expect full utilization. Based on our understanding of the market, as and when we have the capacities, we are looking at able to market it, full utilization of R32.

items.quote: We achieved our highest ever Q1 sales of INR 484 crores with sales volume of 0.85 million square feet. Collections were INR 365 crores, supported by execution and handovers.

items.statement: FY30 ambition remains 2x revenue from FY25 and 3x EBITDA in same period

items.statement: Gross margin at 58.4% in Q1 FY27, down 131 bps YoY due to higher commodity costs and adverse currency
items.quote: Gross margins for the quarter stood at 58.4%, lower by 131 basis points year-on-year, reflecting the impact of higher commodity costs and adverse currency movements.

items.quote: The price increase, the band was roughly between 3% to 12%.

items.quote: At this point in time, we are going to be more measured as far as consumer price increase is concerned because we see a very, very strong tailwind as far as growth is concerned and our bias will be towards not disturbing that.

items.quote: Given that there is a relative softness that we've seen and these are initial signs that we've seen as far as AMC bookings are concerned, that impact would play out towards the later part of the year.

items.quote: At an overall year level, we do expect our A&SP spends to be ahead of revenue growth. So that is something that we are planning for.

items.statement: No current plans for promoter stake increase or strategic investor fundraising; focus remains on business execution.

items.statement: No capex plans for FY27 as of now
items.quote: As far as any CAPEX plans are concerned there is no such CAPEX plan as of yet.

items.quote: We are bidding in Bihar and Madhya Pradesh. And any projects that we see, we are exploring some projects in Maharashtra and Karnataka also.

items.statement: Working capital cycle ~120 days; delays in government payments create cash flow pressure
items.quote: For working capital, definitely once work is stopped due to whatsoever reason, then payment from the government is delayed. And payment from the government is delayed, it hampers the work again.

items.quote: As far as the current numbers are concerned about , so the revenue is about 42% from Uttar Pradesh and about 61% from Uttarakhand as far as these quarters are concerned.

items.quote: I think that will only be achieved from Quarter 3. Because it is a sewerage network project. So, in Quarter 2 also, that revenue cannot be achieved in sewer line projects. But Q3 and Q4 numbers with regard to the Kolkata project would be much better than what you are anticipating.

items.statement: No guidance issued for FY27; management expects to provide guidance next quarter as market stabilizes
items.quote: See, we haven't given any guidance for the current year, Sonal. And at this point as well, we are not really issuing a guidance for the current year. We will evolve and as the market stabilizes, we should hopefully be coming out with the guidance next quarter.

items.quote: we will see margins come back very quickly to the 20-plus percent mark first. And as the business continues to scale, we do feel confident that we'll get back to that 30% aspiration in the mid term. So my sense at this point based on what trending we are seeing is that in the second half of the year, we should start be

items.statement: Q2 FY27 margins expected to improve marginally but remain range-bound; meaningful improvement seen in H2 FY27
items.quote: I think there is a little bit of improvement on account of MICE, but for the second element, which is the capacity still continues to be coming back only gradually. items.statement: MICE operates at 40%+ operating margin vs 15-20% for other businesses; contributes 20-25% of annual profitability; lumpy quarterly nature requires year-on-year view
items.quote: MICE will account for anywhere between 20% to maybe -- on an annual basis, 20%, you might have quarters where it tends to be closer to 25%, but that's about it. It's not that more than 50% of the business would come from MICE.

items.statement: Corporate restructuring (Yatra India merger with parent) ongoing across India, Singapore, Cyprus, Cayman, SEC; no fixed timeline given regulatory complexity
items.quote: having seen how regulators in different markets behave, it's very hard to give an exact timeline on that.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin expansion of 150-200 bps expected vs prior year, above the 100-150 bps annual target
items.quote: this a year where we will clearly do better than that, at least 150 basis points – 200 basis points is what we see us doing you know over last and this year.

items.statement: Calibrated price increases taken end of Q1 to offset packaging cost inflation from crude oil; real gross margin impact expected in Q2
items.quote: we've actually taken calibrated price increases towards the end of Q1, we'll be able to offset any such inflationary impact on our procurement perspective.

items.statement: Focus categories contribution rose to ~85% of revenue in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Now the contribution of focus categories has also increased to almost 85%, in Q1FY '27.

items.statement: Launched FIKN, India's first elixir-based fine fragrance brand with patented design; clinically tested 12-hour stay
items.quote: We finally have launched a brand called FIKN. It's India's first elixir-based brand, which is the highest dosed and the strongest form of perfume that we have brought to India.

items.statement: BTM Ventures (Reginald) ARR grew ~100% post-acquisition to INR 150 cr; expanded to Maharashtra, new category, new channels
items.quote: BTM Ventures, which we acquired in January, it continues to do well. It has reached an ARR of INR150 crores in the last quarter. Since we acquired, we've actually grown it almost 100%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR 8,200-8,300 crores implying 20-25% growth over FY26 INR 6,400 crores
items.quote: This year, we were looking at touching approximately INR8,200 crores, INR8,300 crores. So we'll see close to about 20%, 25% growth.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin expected to reach 4.3-4.4% for FY27, below earlier 5% target due to CV mix shift
items.quote: We would still be in the region of about 4.3%, 4.4% overall for the -- I mean, when we go to Q3, Q4.

items.statement: Acquired businesses expected to achieve sustainable PAT profitability from Q2 FY27 onwards
items.quote: As guided during our previous call, we expect the acquired business to achieve sustainable profitability at the PAT level from Q2 onwards.

items.statement: PV service volume growth of 6-7% expected from Q2 FY27 onwards after Honda divestment impact removed
items.quote: Q2 onwards, we'll see a growth. I wouldn't say 15% growth, which we have guided, but we'll show -- we'll be having a growth of about 6% to 7% in terms of volumes.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 reported EBITDA margin 3.8% vs 2.9% YoY; adjusted EBITDA INR 62 crores up 82% YoY
items.quote: reported EBITDA increased approximately 87% Y-o-Y to INR71.5 crores, with EBITDA margins improving to 3.8% from 2.9% in Q1 last year.

items.statement: PV segment EBITDA margin currently ~4%, expected to inch up from Q2 with Maruti growth and Audi contribution
items.quote: currently, we are at around 4% in terms of PV EBITDA as such. So that should keep inching forward in Q2, Q3 and Q4 with Audi also coming in line.

items.statement: CV EBITDA margin ~3.6-3.7% due to high ticket size (~INR 17 lakh) dragging blended margin lower
items.quote: our CV EBITDA percentage because of the CV ticket size, the ticket size of CVs would be about INR16,00,000 on an average. Our EBITDA margins because of that is about 3.6% to 3.7%

items.statement: CV tipper segment seeing low to negative growth due to construction slowdown; other CV segments holding well
items.quote: the tipper segment in commercial vehicles, we are seeing a low to negative growth in terms of Tipper segment. But the small, intermediate, light commercial vehicles, Cargo segment, all are holding good.

items.statement: Kerala revenue share fell below 50% for first time in Q1 FY27; geographic diversification achieved via FY26 acquisitions
items.quote: In Q1 FY27, the revenue contribution from Kerala m, or Keralam as is now called, declined to below 50% for the first time

items.statement: Capex limited to replacement and ongoing projects; no acquisition-led expansion planned; focus on debt repayment
items.quote: Currently, the only kind of the Capex spend that we have is more in terms of the replacement Capex and the current projects that are in progress. So there's nothing that is really planned in terms of an acquisition kind of an expansion at this point.

items.statement: Spare parts supply constraints causing vehicles stuck in workshops; Ather EV inventory ~5 days; JLR supply constrained
items.quote: On the service side, spare parts remains a concern in terms of supply. So there is a short supply on spare parts, and hence, a lot of vehicles getting stuck in the workshops.

items.statement: Audi new launch expected in Q3 FY27 to drive stronger volumes; Olympus Audi EBITDA neutral in Q1
items.quote: Audi, with the new launch that will happen in Q3, I think stronger numbers would happen in Q3.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 20-25% for FY27 maintained; EBITDA margin guidance of 12-14% for full year maintained
items.quote: Our revenue growth guidance of around 20% to 25% remains intact. We also maintain our full year EBITDA margin guidance of about 12% to 14%.

items.statement: Order book stood at INR 1,801 crores as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: Our order book as on 30th of June 2026 stood at INR 1,801 crores, providing us with a very healthy base of executable projects for the year.

items.statement: Bid pipeline exceeds INR 6,000 crores with 50:50 domestic-international split; expects 20-25% hit rate for FY27 order inflows
items.quote: Our current overall opportunity pipeline is more than INR 6,000 crores with a broadly balanced 50:50% mix between international and domestic opportunities.

items.statement: Targeting 40% revenue from non-heating segments (process plants, metals/minerals, offshore, renewables) in 3-5 years from current ~60% heating focus
items.quote: Coming to around 3 to 5 years, we want to move this non-heating segment to around 40% of our revenue should come from the -- and that is the target we are having.

items.quote: On the export side, Africa remains an important market for us, particularly countries such as Nigeria and Ethiopia, where significant investments are being planned across refining, petrochemicals and fertilizers.

items.quote: Yes, debt raising, I mean, yes, absolutely. I think that's a fair conclusion. But from the contract receipt point of view, we might need a bank guarantee limit enhancement basically.

items.statement: Commodity price fluctuations factored into ongoing project costing; most orders placed on fixed-price basis with sub-vendors, limiting margin impact
items.quote: As far as ongoing projects are concerned, these are already factored in our costing. And most of the orders are already placed, and we placed the order on our sub vendor on a fixed price basis.

items.statement: New non-heating segments (offshore, metals/minerals) expected hit rate of 10-12% initially vs 20-25% for heating; TAM estimated at $300-500M (offshore) and $500M-1B (metals/minerals) in India
items.quote: Here, we are expecting around 10% as our hit ratio, at least to start within the next couple of years.

items.statement: Iraq branch office approved for registration to access oil & gas/refining/petchem opportunities; initial setup as registered office, may expand based on orders
items.quote: Iraq now is -- we are coming up with a lot of projects in oil and gas and refining and petchem and allied areas, which is our core competence as well.

items.statement: BPCL Bina project execution across FY27-FY28; overall EBITDA expected in line with 12-14% guidance; Chemdist gross margins expected ~20%
items.quote: And overall, EBITDA would be in line with whatever we have guided for this year.

items.quote: So a matured store, if we are growing at about 15% to 20% year-on-year, we should be very happy, and that is what we are targeting.

items.statement: Pre-Ind AS gross margin 56-60%, EBITDA margin 11-13% consolidated across formats

items.statement: Manufacturing utilization at 68-70%; can double revenue with current capacity by adding machines
items.quote: Currently, our utilization of our manufacturing facility is at about 68% to 70%. We can easily kind of go up to 2x our revenues in the next coming quarters by kind of recalibrating our factory by adding a few machines if required.

items.quote: We entered our first international market in July, opening Stanley Boutique in Colombo, Sri Lanka. This was achieved through a strategic joint venture with Singer Sri Lanka PLC.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 375.43 crore, up from Rs 200 crore guided in Q4 FY26, with max billing in Q3-Q4 FY27

items.statement: Supply conditions stable, pricing competitive; working with OEMs for timely cost pass-through, input cost movements progressively reflected in pricing
items.quote: During the quarter Q1 of FY27, supply side conditions remained stable while pricing continued to be competitive across key segments. The company continued to work closely with OEMs to ensure timely cost pass through with the impact of input cost movement being progressively reflected in pricing.

items.statement: AI seen as revenue opportunity and productivity booster for Orient, unlike large IT peers who face headcount/revenue pressure

items.statement: Minimum gross margin to survive is 5-6%; most deals exceed this, generating profit
items.quote: To survive in the market, I think 5-6% is the minimum gross margin that we need to earn. That's our operating cost which I can share with you. But most of the deals are beyond that. So, that's where the profit comes in.

items.statement: Management reiterated revenue growth aspiration of 15-20% and EBITDA margin target of 18-20% for FY27.
items.quote: So, I think in last time. Yes, so on the aspiration side, so we had said that on the revenue side, 15% to 20% growth and on the margin side, 18% to 20% is the goal.

items.statement: Company executed LOI to acquire land in Palghar, Maharashtra to build owned facility replacing leased premises, aiming to save ~INR2 cr annual rent and enable 3x scale.
items.quote: We have also executed a letter of intent to acquire a new land situated in Palghar, Maharashtra. This is towards transitioning from our currently leased premises to a newly owned facility, which will enable us to improve the workflow efficiency and better control the cost structure.

items.statement: Plans to invest in new machinery in FY27 to modernize and expand manufacturing capacity across business segments.
items.quote: In FY27, we plan to make investments towards the addition of new machinery to modernize and expand the capacity of our manufacturing capabilities.

items.statement: Appointed new US-based CEO with 32 years medtech/dental experience to strengthen US market leadership and scaling.

items.statement: AI-led automation initiatives underway (AI crowns in beta); initial costs higher but expected to normalize next year, supporting margin expansion.
items.quote: We are doing a lot of AI crowns already in beta AI models. So, there is some cost which is initial, which is coming in, which is slightly higher. But as we scale this up, you know, the cost will become much better.

items.statement: Targeting at least 25% year-on-year volume growth in LPG terminaling
items.quote: We like to at least grow in our volumes 25% year-on-year every year. That's our hope. That's how we work for.

items.statement: INR 10,000 crore capex program expected to be commissioned by March-June 2027
items.quote: So what you said 10,000 crores, I think we should reach by March or worst case June '27. So you will see all of that commissioned and all cylinders firing in '27, '28.

items.statement: Liquid storage capacity to grow from 1.7 to 2.2 million cubic meters in FY27 and near 3 million by FY28
items.quote: We are adding half a million by March, one or two months here and there. Half a million in liquid, another half a million to 1 million in FY28. So we jump from 1.7 to 2.2, 2.2 to maybe close to 3 by FY28 end.

items.statement: $5 billion capex target by 2030-31 funded by mix of debt (max 3.5x EBITDA) and equity (target $2bn net worth)
items.quote: But we, I think still remain very, very positive on that $5 billion capex objective that we have to complete by 2030-'31.

items.statement: 15-year take-or-pay agreement with leading conglomerate for >0.5 MTPA petroleum products at Pipavav rail gantry
items.quote: We have secured a 15-year take-or-pay agreement with a leading conglomerate for petroleum product handling, with committed volumes exceeding 0.5 million metric tons per annum.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin of 76.7% in Q1 FY27, up from prior year
items.quote: This translates into an EBITDA margin of approximately 76.7%, reflecting the strong operating characteristics of our terminaling business and the benefit of additional capacity coming online.

items.statement: LPG throughput tariff standardized at INR 1,175-1,200 per metric ton across all terminals
items.quote: We generally follow a standard rate of INR1,175 across our customer profile. But our principals may pay us a little bit more, maybe INR25 more to at INR1,200.

items.statement: Liquid terminal realization at JNPA of INR 6,000 per CBM vs blended average of INR 3,000
items.quote: You know JNPA gives you a realization of INR6,000 a year against your average blended rate of INR3,000. So that is what makes the difference.

items.statement: Ammonia terminaling realizations 2.5-3x LPG realizations despite lower throughput
items.quote: The realizations are 2.5 to 3 times the LPG realization. So that helps in spite of the lower ton that it is able to do.

items.statement: LPG demand recovery visible with July volumes at 80-85% of normal after geopolitical disruption
items.quote: We are seeing some, sort of, reduction in the shortfall that we have seen month on month. You know, so we in July probably we were down. Now, we are almost just about 80%, 85% of the normal that we were there earlier.

items.statement: Liquid revenue grew 31% YoY driven by new capacity maturation, mix change and higher utilization
items.quote: The growth in liquid terminaling was driven by higher volumes, capacity additions, and a more favorable product mix.

items.statement: Strait of Hormuz disruption risk mitigated by diversified sourcing (Argentina, Canada, USA, Nigeria) and multi-location terminals
items.quote: None of our ships were stuck in Middle East. We always were diversified in our sourcing. We have a very good partner in ITOCHU. We just don't source only from source of convenience.

items.statement: Mandatory 25% public shareholding by June 2028 to support $2bn equity net worth for $5bn capex plan
items.quote: I would almost with my second phase of equity which I have to do mandatorily to dilute to 25% by 2nd June 2028, we are confident that this $2 billion mark, along with this equity infusion and internal accruals, we will be able to reach.

items.statement: Expect high-teens overall volume growth for FY27 including North and GGBS
items.quote: we expect to deliver high teens growth at an overall company basis if I was to include North also as a part of this

items.statement: North operations targeting 60%+ capacity utilization by end of FY27
items.quote: we should be closer to 60% plus by the end of the year in terms of our North operations

items.statement: North plant expected to break even at EBITDA level in Q2 FY27
items.quote: in the second quarter, we should be EBITDA break even

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR2,300 crores for FY27 and INR2,000 crores for FY28
items.quote: this year INR2,300 odd crores, next year INR2,000 crores

items.statement: Long-term capacity expansion from 24.1 MTPA to 43.5 MTPA requiring INR7,500-7,600 crores
items.quote: our intention is to move from 24.1 million currently capacity to about 43.5 over the next few years. Now that requires about INR7,500 crores, INR7,600 crores capex

items.statement: Received approvals for over 29 large infra projects in Q1 FY27 with robust pipeline
items.quote: we have received approvals for over 29 large infra projects in quarter one. Moreover, the project pipeline is also fairly robust

items.statement: North-South cement profitability difference estimated at INR600-700 per ton
items.quote: The difference can be in the range of probably INR600 to INR700 per ton

items.statement: Expect fuel cost to remain flat in Q2 FY27 and decline from Q3 FY27 with domestic coal switch
items.quote: second quarter will be almost same as the first quarter, but going into the third quarter, we expect the cost to come down for us

items.statement: Cement trade mix stable at 51%, clinker-to-cement factor increased to 55% with North launch
items.quote: Within cement, trade mix remains stable at 51%. Our clinker to cement factor increased to 55% with the launch of North operations

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA target maintained below 3.0x per board guidance
items.quote: the internal guidance for us from the board is to keep it below 3.0x

items.statement: PBT margin guidance of 14-16% for near term; aspiration to reach 17-19% beyond 2028 after new plant commissioning
items.quote: I would say we are being conservative. We are -- our aspiration or ambition is to try and get closer to 17, 18 or even 19. In the near term, as we -- investments, make investments, we think that there will be dip, right? Beyond 2028, we would start seeing this improvements.

items.statement: Planning INR 900-950 crore investment for new state-of-the-art Pune plant, production expected from 2028
items.quote: The sharper capital allocation enables making the investment plans we are making in terms of INR900 crores to INR950 crores we are planning to invest to make the new Pune plant, state-of-the-art Pune plant. items.statement: Won INR 140 crore gearbox order (1-year supply) and INR 35 crore tractor OEM order; order book growing sustainably
items.quote: we just won a significant order with a gearbox manufacturer, INR140 crores order, which will help us significantly in our sales in the next few quarters, continuing to next year. Similarly, in agricultural, we just won a INR 35 crores contract with a leading tractor OEM

items.statement: Additional TRB channel to be added by early 2027; most new capacity tied to new Pune factory commissioning in 2028
items.quote: we are also -- again, even though we are constrained by capacity, we are still going to add one additional channel by early 2027, one additional TRB channel by 2027.

items.quote: Mr. Sujeeth Pai, who will be taking over as Managing Director of SKF India Industrial effective September 1st, as you see in the SEBI announcement, as I step into a role to manage the larger region for Industrial Region of India, Southeast Asia & Middle East within SKF Group.

items.statement: Pithampur facility on track for commercial ramp-up from Q1 CY2027; significant expansion headroom on ~30-acre site with only 5-6 acres utilized
items.quote: We are on track to ramp up commercial operations at this facility from first quarter of calendar year 2027 as we had previously guided.

items.statement: Gross margin improved sequentially by ~140 bps to 67.7% despite higher input and freight costs; achieved by exiting lower-margin contract manufacturing
items.quote: Our gross margin increased sequentially by around 140 bps to 67.7%. This is despite we have had sequential increase in key input cost, freight cost due to the geopolitical conditions.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 tracking strong for sequential USD revenue growth after tactical measures in Q1 to improve gross margin mix
items.quote: But Q2 FY27 is tracking strong for sequential USD revenue growth.

items.quote: We received two approvals in this quarter. The commercialization rate remains strong at 88%. Some of these products need to be commercialized in the coming two quarters.

items.statement: Pithampur FDA inspection resulted in 2 procedural observations; response filed and FDA approval received on regulatory filing post-inspection
items.quote: A 483 was issued with two observations which we had said we were confident of concluding the evaluation in a timely way. The observations were procedural.
